definition_zh: 保存；保护；维持；果酱；自然保护区；专属领域
definition_en: to keep something in its original state, or to protect it from harm or change
core_image: 一排玻璃罐把夏天的果子封在糖水里，罐外的果园已经落光了叶子
scene: 果园早已光秃，玻璃罐却把夏天的收成保存了下来。 Glass jars preserve the summer harvest long after the orchard is bare.
sceneCN: 这里 preserve 指「用糖或盐把食物处理过，使其长期不坏」（第 5 个义项：以糖渍、腌渍等方式保存食物）；句意为果园早已光秃，玻璃罐仍封着夏天的收成。图中可辨识物件：玻璃罐、糖汁、果块、贴着手写日期的标签；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 保存；保护；维持；腌制（食物）
蜜饯；果酱（常用复数）；自然保护区；专属领域

senses.title: Keep something from decaying
senses.definition: to treat or store something so that it does not decay
senses.definitionCN: 通过处理或存放使某物不腐坏
senses.example: Salt and smoke preserve meat through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 盐与烟熏能让肉在整个冬天不坏。
senses.why: prae- 'before' plus servare 'keep' gives 'keep beforehand', and keeping food before it spoils is the oldest use of the word.
senses.whyCN: prae-「在前」加 servare「守住」得到「提前守住」，在食物变坏之前先护住，正是这个词最古老的用法。

senses.title: Protect a place from destruction
senses.titleCN: 保护地点、建筑不遭破坏或改造
senses.definition: to protect a building, place or object from being destroyed or altered
senses.definitionCN: 保护建筑、地点或物件不被摧毁或改动
senses.example: The trust preserves the medieval bridge exactly as it stands.
senses.exampleCN: 该信托机构让这座中世纪桥原样留存。
senses.why: the object sense keeps the core meaning untouched: what is preserved is not repaired into something new but kept as it was.
senses.whyCN: 物件义保持了核心含义：被 preserve 的不是被修成新东西，而是按原样留住。

senses.title: Keep a state or quality in being
senses.titleCN: 维持某种状态或品质继续存在
senses.definition: to keep a condition, quality or state continuing
senses.definitionCN: 使某种状况、品质或状态持续下去
senses.example: Officers preserved order while the crowd pushed forward.
senses.exampleCN: 人群向前涌时，警员维持着秩序。
senses.why: order is something that disappears unless it is actively kept, so the verb is used for conditions that need guarding.
senses.whyCN: 秩序若不主动守住就会消失，因此这个词也用于需要守护的状态。

senses.title: Keep something for later generations
senses.titleCN: 为后世留存记录或实物
senses.definition: to keep records, objects or knowledge so that people in the future can still use them
senses.definitionCN: 保存记录、实物或知识，使后人仍能使用
senses.example: Archivists preserve recordings of dialects that no longer have young speakers.
senses.exampleCN: 档案人员保存那些已无年轻使用者的方言录音。
senses.why: here the word looks forward: what is kept now is kept for a time the keeper will never see.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词朝向未来：此刻守住的东西，是为守者永远看不到的时代而留。

senses.title: Prepare fruit or meat with sugar or brine
senses.titleCN: 用糖渍、盐腌等方式加工食物
senses.definition: to prepare fruit or other food with sugar, salt or vinegar so that it keeps
senses.definitionCN: 用糖、盐或醋处理水果等食物以延长保存期
senses.example: Glass jars preserve the summer harvest long after the orchard is bare.
senses.exampleCN: 果园早已光秃，玻璃罐仍封着夏天的收成。
senses.why: the cooking sense specializes the general one: sugar and salt are the agents that do the guarding.
senses.whyCN: 烹调用法是一般义的具体化：糖与盐就是执行「守住」的媒介。

senses.title: A protected area of land
senses.definition: an area of land set aside so that its wildlife or landscape is protected
senses.definitionCN: 为保护野生生物或景观而划出的土地
senses.example: The marsh is a private preserve where hunting is banned.
senses.exampleCN: 这片沼泽是私人保护区，禁止狩猎。
senses.why: the noun turns the act into a place: land where protection happens all the time.
senses.whyCN: 名词义把动作变成地点：持续进行保护的那片土地。

senses.title: Fruit jam in a jar
senses.titleCN: 果酱、蜜饯（美式常用复数）
senses.definition: fruit cooked with sugar and stored in jars
senses.definitionCN: 加糖熬煮后装罐的水果制品
senses.example: She opened a jar of strawberry preserves for the toast.
senses.exampleCN: 她开了一罐草莓酱配吐司。
senses.why: the product noun is inherited straight from the verb, and American English prefers the plural for the jars on the shelf.
senses.whyCN: 成品名词直接承自动词，美式英语更常用复数指架上的那些罐子。

senses.title: An activity reserved for one group
senses.titleCN: 某一群体独占的领域或活动
senses.definition: an activity or area that one group keeps for itself and others are shut out of
senses.definitionCN: 某一群体留给自己、他人不得进入的活动或领域
senses.example: Editing the paper is no longer a male preserve.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑这家报纸不再是男性的专属领域。
senses.why: the idea of keeping something safe for oneself shades easily into keeping others out, which is how this social sense arose.
senses.whyCN: 把某物为自己守住，很容易滑向把别人挡在外面，这个社会义就是这样产生的。

intro.en: Preserve comes through Old French from Latin praeservare, built on prae- 'before' and servare 'to keep'. It shares its root with conserve but not its prefix. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: preserve 经古法语来自拉丁 praeservare，由 prae-「在前」与 servare「守住」构成。它与 conserve 共享词根，但前缀不同。年代均为约数。

items.en: Prae- meant 'before, in front of', and in compounds it often adds the idea of doing something in advance.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在……之前」，在复合词中常添「预先」的意思。

items.en: Praeservare meant 'to keep or guard beforehand', a combination of the prefix with servare 'to keep safe'.
items.cn: praeservare 意为「提前看守、预先保住」，是前缀与 servare「守住」的组合。

items.en: Old French preserver brought the word into English in the fourteenth century, and the spelling settled as preserve.
items.cn: 古法语 preserver 在 14 世纪把词带入英语，拼写最终固定为 preserve。

items.en: The food sense is recorded from the sixteenth century; the sense of land set aside for wildlife developed in the nineteenth, when the first large reserves were mapped.
items.cn: 食物义在 16 世纪有记录；为野生生物划出土地的意思在 19 世纪形成，当时最早的几处大型保护区被勘定。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest citation for the jam noun and for the nature-reserve sense is not precisely recorded, and the pre-Latin origin of servare remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：果酱名词义与自然保护区义的最早书证没有确切记录；servare 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds verbs that share the Latin -serve stock and are easily mistaken; group two holds words that also mean keeping something safe but differ in emphasis.
note.cn: 第一组是共享拉丁 -serve 词干、容易认错的动词；第二组同样表示「保住」，但侧重点不同。

entries.definition: Com- plus servare stresses keeping a resource from being used up; preserve stresses keeping something from changing or spoiling.
entries.definitionCN: com- 加 servare 强调不让资源被用尽；preserve 强调不让某物改变或变坏。

entries.definition: Re- 'back' plus servare: to set something aside instead of using it now, as in reserve a table.
entries.definitionCN: re-「向后」加 servare：把某物留到以后再用，如预订餐桌。

entries.definition: Ob- 'toward' plus servare: to watch, notice, or follow a rule; nothing is being stored.
entries.definitionCN: ob-「朝向」加 servare：观看、察觉或遵守规则；并不涉及储存。

entries.definition: De- 'fully' plus servire 'to serve': to have earned something. Same look, different root.
entries.definitionCN: de-「完全」加 servire「服侍」：因服务而应得。形似而词根不同。

entries.definition: To keep something safe from active harm; it says nothing about keeping it unchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物免受主动伤害；不涉及保持原样。

entries.definition: To keep something one already has, such as heat or a right, without the idea of guarding it.
entries.definitionCN: 指继续保有已拥有之物，如热量或权利，不含守护之意。

entries.definition: To use a resource sparingly so that it lasts; its focus is quantity, not condition.
entries.definitionCN: 节制使用资源使其持久；关注的是数量而非状态。

entries.definition: To keep something working by servicing it, as a machine; preserve does not imply repair.
entries.definitionCN: 通过保养使某物继续运转，如机器；preserve 不含修理之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: prae- 'before' + servare 'keep': guard it before harm arrives.
normal.cn: prae-「在前」+ servare「守住」：在伤害到来之前先护住。

normal.en: The family runs preserve, preservation, preservative, preserver, preservationist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 preserve、preservation、preservative、preserver、preservationist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: preserve food, preserve order, nature preserve, fruit preserves.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：保存食物、维持秩序、自然保护区、果酱。

normal.en: The root is shared with conserve and reserve, but the prefixes do the dividing.
normal.cn: 词根与 conserve、reserve 共享，靠前缀区分。

normal.en: American English says preserves for jam, British English often says jam.
normal.cn: 美式英语用 preserves 指果酱，英式英语常用 jam。

abstract.en: Picture a jar of summer standing on a shelf in January.
abstract.cn: 想象一月的架子上摆着一罐夏天。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge left exactly as it was, weeds and all.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥连杂草都原样留着。

abstract.en: Picture a fence that keeps a meadow for animals and people out of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一道篱笆把草场留给动物，把人挡在外面。

examples.en: The museum preserves the letters in acid-free boxes.
examples.cn: 博物馆把信件放在无酸盒中保存。

examples.en: Freezing preserves the flavour far better than drying.
examples.cn: 冷冻保存风味远胜于干燥。

examples.en: The old quarter is preserved as a living neighbourhood, not a museum.
examples.cn: 这片老城区是作为活着的社区被保护，而不是当成博物馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pre（提前）+ serve（守住）」——在坏掉之前先护住 → 保存、保护、维持

root: 拉丁 praeservare「提前守住」= prae-（在前）+ servare「看守、保存」；与 conserve 共享 servare 词根，靠前缀区分。英语 preserve。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: something is guarded before harm reaches it, and that guard is then applied to food, buildings, order, records, land, jam and finally to a social boundary.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：在损害到达之前先护住某物，这道防护再依次用于食物、建筑、秩序、记录、土地、果酱，最后用于一条社会边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a jar and a fence, both keeping something whole against time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只罐与一道篱笆，都在对抗时间地把某物完整留住。

branches.en: STOP DECAY: sugar, salt and smoke are the guard, whether in a pot or a jar.
branches.cn: 止住腐坏：糖、盐与烟就是那道防护，无论在锅里还是罐里。

branches.en: UNCHANGED OBJECT: a building is kept as it stands, not restored into something new.
branches.cn: 原样的物件：建筑按现状留住，而不是修成新东西。

branches.en: STATE AND RECORD: order and archives both vanish unless someone keeps them.
branches.cn: 状态与记录：秩序与档案若无人守护都会消失。

branches.en: SET ASIDE: the act becomes a place, and the product becomes a jar.
branches.cn: 留出：动作变成一片地，成品变成一罐酱。

branches.en: KEPT FOR SOME: guarding something for oneself ends by shutting others out.
branches.cn: 为某些人留住：为自己守住，最终把别人挡在外面。

intro.en: Preserve is a Latin verb of prefix plus root; the same two parts build conserve, reserve and observe, so the family is best read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: preserve 是由前缀加词根构成的拉丁动词；同样的两部分也构成 conserve、reserve 与 observe，因此这个词族最好按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- 'before' and servare 'to keep' give praeservare; English draws preserve, preservation, preservative and preserver from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 prae-「在前」与 servare「守住」构成 praeservare；英语由此得到 preserve、preservation、preservative 与 preserver。

items.example: The prefix marks action taken ahead of time.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记提前采取的行动。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of guarding.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供「守护」的意思。

items.example: Salt preserves the fish before it spoils.
items.exampleCN: 盐在鱼变坏之前先把它保住。

items.example: Cold storage aids the preservation of vaccines.
items.exampleCN: 冷藏有助于疫苗的保存。

items.meaning: a substance that keeps food from spoiling
items.meaningCN: 防止食物变坏的添加物
items.example: The label lists no preservatives.
items.exampleCN: 标签上未列出任何防腐剂。

items.meaning: a person or thing that preserves
items.example: He was a preserver of local songs.
items.exampleCN: 他是当地歌谣的保存者。

items.example: Dried grain is preservable for years.
items.exampleCN: 干燥的谷物可保存多年。

items.meaning: an advocate of protecting old buildings or land
items.meaningCN: 主张保护老建筑或土地的人
items.example: Preservationists fought the demolition.
items.exampleCN: 保护主义者反对这次拆除。

items.example: They reserved two rooms for the wedding.
items.exampleCN: 他们为婚礼留了两间房。

latinEntries.meaning: to keep beforehand, protect in advance

definition_zh: 方式；模式；交通方式；生产方式；时尚；调式；语气；众数
definition_en: a way in which something is done, operates, or exists; also a prevailing fashion, a musical scale, a grammatical mood, or the most frequent value in a set
core_image: 一把尺子量出恰好的一段，再照这个尺寸去做
scene: 出行方案表里列了地铁、公交、骑车和步行四种方式，让人比较城市负担得起哪一种。 The transport plan lists four modes — metro, bus, bicycle and walking — and asks which one the city can afford.
sceneCN: 这里 mode 是「交通方式」（第 3 个义项：交通方式）；句意：这份交通规划列出四种方式——地铁、公交、自行车和步行——并追问这座城市负担得起哪一种。场景要点：一张摊开的城市交通图、四条并排的路线、被圈出的预算数字；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 方式；模式；样式；调式；语气；众数

senses.title: A way of doing
senses.definition: the particular way in which someone does something or something happens
senses.definitionCN: 某人做某事或某事发生的特定方式
senses.example: Her mode of working is to write everything by hand before typing it.
senses.exampleCN: 她的工作方式是先把一切手写下来，再打字。
senses.why: Latin modus is a measure. A way of doing something is the measure the action is cut to, so the word begins as the shape given to an activity rather than its purpose.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 modus 是“尺度”。做某事的方式，就是动作被裁成的尺寸，因此这个词的起点是给一项活动定形，而不是给它定目的。

senses.title: A machine setting
senses.definition: one of the fixed settings in which a machine or system can operate
senses.definitionCN: 机器或系统可以运行的固定设置之一
senses.example: At ten the alarm switches itself into night mode.
senses.exampleCN: 到了十点，警报器会自动切换到夜间模式。
senses.why: A machine repeats the same operations, and each setting is a measure it can be set to. The word moves from human ways of acting to the repeatable ways a device acts.
senses.whyCN: 机器重复同样的操作，每一种设置都是它可以被调到的某个尺度。这个词从人的行事方式，转到设备可重复的运行方式。

senses.title: A way to travel
senses.definition: a particular means or system of moving people or goods, such as rail, road, air, or water
senses.definitionCN: 运送人或货物的特定手段或系统，如铁路、公路、航空或水运
senses.example: Rail is still the cheapest mode of transport for coal.
senses.exampleCN: 对煤炭来说，铁路仍是最便宜的运输方式。
senses.why: Transport is measured out by the vehicle and the route chosen. The fixed phrase 'mode of transport' treats each means of travel as one measured option among several.
senses.whyCN: 运输由所选的交通工具与路线量定。固定短语“mode of transport”把每一种出行手段都当作若干被量定的选项之一。

senses.title: A way of producing
senses.definition: the organized way in which a society or economy makes goods, especially in economic and historical writing
senses.definitionCN: 社会或经济制造商品的有机组织方式，尤用于经济与历史写作
senses.example: The factory changed the mode of production from batch work to a moving line.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂把生产方式从分批作业改成了流水线。
senses.why: Economics borrowed the measure for the whole arrangement of work: tools, labour, and ownership fitted together into one measured pattern of making things.
senses.whyCN: 经济学借用了这个“尺度”，用来指整个劳动安排：工具、劳动力与所有权被合成一个被量定的制造格局。

senses.title: The prevailing fashion
senses.definition: the current fashion or style, especially in dress, in somewhat formal or old-fashioned use
senses.definitionCN: 当下的风尚或款式，尤指服饰，语气较正式或略显旧式
senses.example: Narrow coats were the mode in the winter of that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那年冬天，窄身大衣正是风尚。
senses.why: French mode means fashion, a specialized use of the same word. Fashion is the measure everyone agrees to wear for a season, so the sense of 'current style' grows straight out of 'measure'.
senses.whyCN: 法语 mode 意为“时尚”，是同一个词的专门用法。时尚就是大家在一季里共同同意穿着的尺度，所以“当下款式”这一义项直接从“尺度”长出来。

senses.title: A musical mode
senses.definition: a pattern of intervals used to organize a melody, especially one of the ancient or church modes
senses.definitionCN: 用来组织旋律的音程模式，尤指古代调式或教会调式
senses.example: The second movement is built on an old church mode rather than a major key.
senses.exampleCN: 第二乐章建立在古老的教会调式上，而不是大调上。
senses.why: Latin modus also meant rhythm and song. Musicians divide the octave by a measured pattern, and that pattern of intervals is literally the measure of the melody.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 modus 也指节奏与歌曲。音乐家按一种被量定的模式划分八度，这种音程模式字面上就是旋律的尺度。

senses.title: A grammatical mood
senses.definition: the form of a verb that shows whether it states, commands, wishes, or supposes
senses.definitionCN: 动词的形式，表明它是在陈述、命令、祝愿还是假设
senses.example: In Latin the verb's mode tells whether it states a fact or gives an order.
senses.exampleCN: 在拉丁语中，动词的语气表明它是在陈述事实还是下达命令。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word for the form that measures the speaker's attitude toward the action. Late Latin used modus for this category, and English kept it beside the more common 'mood'.
senses.whyCN: 语法学借用了这个词，指量定说话人对动作态度的形式。晚期拉丁语用 modus 指这一范畴，英语把它与更常见的 mood 并留着。

senses.title: The statistical mode
senses.definition: in statistics, the value that occurs most frequently in a set of data
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中在一组数据里出现次数最多的值
senses.example: In this data set the mode is 4, because 4 appears more often than any other value.
senses.exampleCN: 在这组数据中，众数是 4，因为 4 出现的次数比其他任何值都多。
senses.why: Statistics keeps the old sense of measure but points it at frequency: the mode is the value where the data pile up, the measure at which the set is most itself.
senses.whyCN: 统计学保留了这个词古老的“尺度”义，却把它指向频次：众数是数据堆积之处，是这组数据最像自己的那个尺度。

senses.title: A whole way of being
senses.definition: a general state or manner of existence, as in 'survival mode' or 'a mode of life'
senses.definitionCN: 总体的存在状态或生活方式，如“survival mode”或“a mode of life”
senses.example: During the storm the crew went into survival mode and stopped all repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨期间，船员进入求生模式，停止了所有修理。
senses.why: The measure can be applied to a whole life, not just one action. A mode of being is the overall pattern a person or group is currently cut to.
senses.whyCN: 这个尺度可以被用在整整一种生活上，而不只是一个动作。存在方式，就是一个人或群体当下被裁成的总体格局。

intro.en: Mode comes from Latin modus 'measure' through French, and the same measure runs through music, grammar, fashion, economics, and statistics. Its look-alike mood is a different word. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mode 经法语来自拉丁语 modus“尺度”，同一把尺子贯穿音乐、语法、时尚、经济与统计。与它形近的 mood 是另一个词。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Mode is first recorded in English meaning 'melodies, strains of music', a sense now obsolete. It came from Old French mode and directly from Latin modus.
items.cn: mode 在英语中最早记录为“旋律、乐曲”，这一义项今已废弃。它来自古法语 mode，并直接来自拉丁语 modus。

items.en: Latin modus meant 'measure, extent, quantity; proper measure, rhythm, song; a way, manner, fashion, style', and in Late Latin also 'mood' in grammar and logic.
items.cn: 拉丁语 modus 意为“尺度、范围、数量；恰当的尺度、节奏、歌曲；方式、做法、样式、风格”，在晚期拉丁语中还指语法与逻辑中的“语气”。

items.en: Modus goes back to PIE *med- 'take appropriate measures'. The same root lies behind moderate, modest, modify, model, modern, and medicine.
items.cn: modus 可追溯到原始印欧语 *med-“采取恰当的尺度”。同一词根也是 moderate、modest、modify、model、modern、medicine 的来源。

items.en: A second French borrowing gives mode the sense 'current fashion, prevailing style' (1640s). The central sense 'manner of acting or doing, the way in which a thing is done' is recorded by the 1660s.
items.cn: 另一次法语借入使 mode 获得“当下时尚、流行款式”之义（17 世纪 40 年代）。核心义“行事方式、做一件事的方式”到 17 世纪 60 年代才有记录。

items.en: The grammatical sense 'inflectional category in conjugation' is mid-15c. In music, mode is recorded from the 1670s for the Greek method of dividing the octave, and by 1721 for modern music.
items.cn: 语法义“变位中的屈折范畴”出现于 15 世纪中叶。音乐中，mode 于 17 世纪 70 年代指希腊人划分八度的方法，到 1721 年指现代音乐中的调式。

items.en: Mood 'state of mind' (c. 1300) comes from Old English mod 'heart, frame of mind', a word of unknown origin, and has no etymological link with mode. Grammatical mood (1570s) is a different word again: it is an alteration of mode.
items.cn: mood“心境”（约 1300）来自古英语 mod“心、心境”，词源不明，与 mode 没有词源关系。语法上的 mood（16 世纪 70 年代）又是另一个词：它是 mode 的变体拼写。

note.en: The first group separates mode from the look-alikes built on the same or a neighbouring stem; the second compares the ordinary words for 'the way something is done'.
note.cn: 第一组把 mode 与同词干或邻近词干的形近词分开；第二组比较表示“做事的方式”的常用词。

entries.tag: state of mind not from modus
entries.definition: a temporary state of mind or feeling. It comes from Old English mod, not from Latin modus. Only the grammatical mood is a different word, an alteration of mode.
entries.definitionCN: 暂时的心境或情绪。它来自古英语 mod，而不是拉丁语 modus。只有语法上的 mood 是另一个词，即 mode 的变体。

entries.definition: a small representation or an example to copy. It goes back to Latin modellus, a diminutive of modus, so it is 'a little measure' rather than a way of acting.
entries.definitionCN: 小型的代表物或供模仿的范例。它可追溯到拉丁语 modellus，即 modus 的指小形式，所以它是“一个小小的尺度”，而不是行事方式。

entries.definition: relating to mode, especially in grammar, music, or logic. It is the adjective; mode is the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 与 mode 有关的，尤用于语法、音乐或逻辑。它是形容词，mode 是名词。

entries.definition: fashionable, often with a hint of contempt. It is built from mode in its 'fashion' sense plus -ish.
entries.definitionCN: 时髦的，常带一丝轻蔑。它由表示“时尚”的 mode 加 -ish 构成。

entries.definition: a planned and organized procedure for doing something, often teachable step by step. A mode is the shape of the doing; a method is the route with steps.
entries.definitionCN: 为做某事而计划的、有组织的程序，通常可以一步步传授。mode 是做法呈现的形态，method 是带步骤的路线。

entries.definition: the way in which something is done, often with attention to style or bearing. It is close to mode but more personal and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的方式，常带有风格或举止的意味。它接近 mode，但更个人化，技术性更弱。

entries.definition: the most general word for how something is done. It can replace mode in most everyday sentences, though not in fixed terms such as mode of production.
entries.definitionCN: 表示“如何做”的最通用词。它在多数日常句子里可以替换 mode，但不能替换 mode of production 这类固定说法。

entries.definition: a prevailing custom or style, and also 'in the manner of'. It overlaps with mode in the sense 'current style', but mode is far more formal there.
entries.definitionCN: 流行风俗或款式，也可表示“以……的方式”。它在“当下款式”一义上与 mode 重叠，但 mode 在该义上正式得多。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin modus 'measure', the PIE root *med-, and the English family modal, modality, model, and modify.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 modus“尺度”、原始印欧语词根 *med-，以及英语词族 modal、modality、model、modify。

normal.en: modus is Latin for 'measure'. A mode is the measure an action is cut to, which is why the word covers ways, settings, and styles at once.
normal.cn: modus 是拉丁语的“尺度”。mode 就是一个动作被裁成的尺寸，所以这个词同时覆盖方式、设置与款式。

normal.en: The fixed phrases keep the measure visible: mode of transport, mode of production, mode of operation.
normal.cn: 固定短语把“尺度”保留在明面上：交通方式、生产方式、运作方式。

normal.en: mood 'state of mind' is not related: it comes from Old English mod. Only grammatical mood is a variant of mode.
normal.cn: mood“心境”与它无关：它来自古英语 mod。只有语法上的 mood 才是 mode 的变体。

normal.en: model is a 'little measure' (Latin modellus), a pattern to copy, not a way of doing.
normal.cn: model 是“小小的尺度”（拉丁语 modellus），指供模仿的范本，而不是行事方式。

normal.en: modal, modality, and multimodal all keep the noun's stem; they describe the form or the channel, not the fashion.
normal.cn: modal、modality、multimodal 都保留了这个名词的词干；它们描述形式或通道，而不指时尚。

abstract.en: Picture a tailor's ruler laid on cloth. The ruler does not decide what the cloth is for; it only fixes the shape. Mode is that ruler applied to an action.
abstract.cn: 想象一把裁缝尺压在布上。尺子不决定布用来做什么，只固定形状。mode 就是那把量在动作上的尺子。

abstract.en: A switch with several positions is a row of modes: each position is a stable measure the machine can return to.
abstract.cn: 一个有多个挡位的开关就是一排模式：每个挡位都是机器可以回到的稳定尺度。

abstract.en: Fashion is a measure everyone agrees to wear for a season; that is why the same word can mean 'way' and 'style'.
abstract.cn: 时尚就是大家在一季里共同同意穿着的尺度；正因如此，同一个词既能指“方式”，又能指“款式”。

examples.en: The city's buses and trains are two modes of the same public transport system.
examples.cn: 城市的公交与地铁是同一套公共交通系统里的两种方式。

examples.en: Please leave the phone in silent mode during the examination.
examples.cn: 考试期间请把手机留在静音模式。

examples.en: The historian argues that a new mode of production changed the family as well as the factory.
examples.cn: 这位历史学家主张，新的生产方式不仅改变了工厂，也改变了家庭。

dict_mnemonic.text: “摸的”——先摸清门道，量好尺寸再动手，什么东西就按什么方式做 → mode 方式、模式（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 modus“尺度、方式”，核心是“按一把量好的尺子去做，形成固定的做法”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of mode, all cut from one measure: a ruler that fixes the shape of an action, a machine setting, a melody, a verb form, or a whole way of life.
sensesIntro.cn: mode 的九个义项都从同一把尺子上裁下：它固定一个动作、一个设备设置、一段旋律、一种动词形式或一整种生活形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler laid on something to fix its shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子压在事物上，固定它的形状。

branches.en: MEASURE APPLIED: a human action takes a shape, and a machine takes a repeatable setting.
branches.cn: 尺度落下：人的动作被定形，机器被调到一个可重复的设置。

branches.en: ORGANIZED MEANS: transport and production each settle into a measured arrangement of vehicles, tools, and labour.
branches.cn: 有组织的手段：运输与生产各自固定成由车辆、工具与劳动组成的被量定安排。

branches.en: STYLE AND SONG: the measure becomes the fashion of a season and the interval pattern of a melody.
branches.cn: 款式与歌曲：这把尺子变成一季的时尚，也变成旋律的音程模式。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: the verb's form is the measure of the speaker's attitude.
branches.cn: 语法：动词的形式成为说话人态度的尺度。

branches.en: DATA AND LIFE: the mode is where data pile up, and a mode of life is the whole pattern a person is cut to.
branches.cn: 数据与生活：众数是数据堆积之处，而生活方式是一个人被裁成的整体格局。

intro.en: Mode is a Latin noun, and mod- is one of the most productive stems in English: -al, -ality, -ish, -ern, -el, -ule, -ify and multi- all attach to it.
intro.cn: mode 是拉丁语名词，mod- 是英语里最能产出的词干之一：-al、-ality、-ish、-ern、-el、-ule、-ify 与 multi- 都能接在它上面。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is modus 'measure', with diminutives modulus and modellus and the verb moderari 'keep within measure'. All of them keep the idea of a fixed proportion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基是 modus“尺度”，另有指小形式 modulus 与 modellus，以及动词 moderari“保持在尺度之内”。它们都保留“固定比例”的意思。

items.meaningCN: 方式；模式（拉丁语“尺度、方式”）
items.example: The app has a simple mode for beginners.
items.exampleCN: 这个应用为初学者设有一个简单模式。

items.meaning: relating to mode, mood, or form
items.meaningCN: 模态的；语气的（mod- 尺度 + -al 形容词后缀）
items.example: The grammar lesson covers modal verbs such as 'can' and 'must'.
items.exampleCN: 这堂语法课讲 can、must 这类情态动词。

items.meaning: a mode or channel of something
items.meaningCN: 模态；形式；感觉通道（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The study compares visual and auditory modalities.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究比较视觉与听觉通道。

items.meaningCN: 多模态的（multi- 多 + modal 模态的）
items.example: The course uses a multimodal approach with text, sound, and images.
items.exampleCN: 这门课采用文字、声音与图像的多模态方法。

items.meaningCN: 时髦的（mode 时尚 + -ish 形容词后缀）
items.example: The room was furnished in a modish style that dated quickly.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间按一种很快过时的时髦风格布置。

items.meaning: no longer in fashion or use
items.meaningCN: 过时的（out- 超出 + mode 款式 + -ed）
items.example: The factory still runs on outmoded equipment.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂仍在用过时的设备运转。

items.meaningCN: 模型；范本（mod- 尺度 + -el 指小后缀）
items.example: They built a scale model of the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 他们制作了这座桥的比例模型。

items.meaningCN: 现代的（-ern 构成形容词）
items.example: Modern offices rarely keep paper files.
items.exampleCN: 现代办公室很少保存纸质档案。

items.meaningCN: 适度的；使缓和（保持在应有尺度内）
items.example: The region has a moderate climate.
items.exampleCN: 这个地区气候温和。

items.meaning: to change in measure or detail
items.example: The engineers modified the valve to reduce flow.
items.exampleCN: 工程师改动了阀门以减少流量。

items.meaningCN: 模块；单元（mod- 尺度 + -ule 指小后缀）
items.example: The software is built from reusable modules.
items.exampleCN: 这个软件由可复用的模块构成。

items.meaning: to adjust in measure, tone, or strength
items.meaningCN: 调节；调制（按小尺度调整）
items.example: She modulated her voice so as not to wake the baby.
items.exampleCN: 她压低并调节了声音，以免吵醒婴儿。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 小尺度；范本（modus 的指小形式）

definition_zh: 定罪；判罪；坚定信念
definition_en: a court decision that someone is guilty, or a strong and steady belief
core_image: 一纸判决放在桌上，胸口另有一只手始终不肯松开
scene: 宣判之后，她仍抬起头，说自己相信这条路是对的。 She spoke with the conviction of someone who had waited years.
sceneCN: 这里 conviction 指「坚定信念」（第 2 个义项：深信不疑的看法）；句意是她说话时带着一种等了多年的坚定信念。

senses.title: A court ruling of guilt
senses.definition: an official decision that a person is guilty of a crime
senses.definitionCN: 正式认定某人犯有某项罪行的决定
senses.example: The conviction was overturned on appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 这项定罪在上诉时被推翻了。
senses.why: A single ruling can follow a person for the rest of a life.
senses.whyCN: 一次裁决可能跟着一个人走过余生。

senses.title: A steady belief
senses.definition: a firm belief that something is true or right
senses.definitionCN: 坚信某事为真或为对的看法
senses.example: She lives by the conviction that work should be fair.
senses.exampleCN: 她秉持工作应当公平的信念生活。
senses.why: A belief that survives argument is held by something stronger than habit.
senses.whyCN: 经得住争辩的信念，靠的比习惯更结实。

intro.en: Conviction comes from Latin convictio, a proving of guilt, from convincere, to overcome with proof, built from com-, together, and vincere, to conquer.
intro.cn: conviction 来自拉丁语 convictio（证明有罪），源于 convincere（用证据驳倒），由 com-（一起）与 vincere（征服）构成。

items.en: Vincere meant to conquer and to carry the day.
items.cn: vincere 意为征服、占上风。

items.en: Convincere meant to overcome a person by clear proof.
items.cn: convincere 意为用清楚的证据把人驳倒。

items.en: Convictio named both the proof and the state of being proven wrong.
items.cn: convictio 既指证据，也指被证明有错的状态。

items.en: English conviction first meant the proving of guilt.
items.cn: 英语 conviction 最初指对罪行的证明。

items.en: The same word came to mean a belief held beyond doubt.
items.cn: 同一个词开始表示不容怀疑的信念。

items.en: Law keeps the first sense, while daily speech keeps the second.
items.cn: 法律保留了第一个义项，日常口语保留了第二个。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin conquering base vict-, and the meaning group names other words for belief and for legal decisions.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的征服词基 vict-，近义组列出其他表示信念与法律裁决的词。

entries.definition: to find someone guilty in court
entries.definitionCN: 在法庭上判定某人有罪

entries.definition: to make someone feel sure
entries.definitionCN: 使某人确信

entries.definition: the act of forcing someone out of a place
entries.definitionCN: 把人赶出某地的行为

entries.definition: a feeling that something is true
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事为真的感觉

entries.definition: a state of being completely sure
entries.definitionCN: 完全确定的状态

entries.definition: the punishment given by a court
entries.definitionCN: 法庭给出的刑罚

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a verdict written down, then move to a belief that cannot be argued away.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一纸写下的判决开始，再到一个争辩不掉的信念。

normal.en: Convict is the act and conviction is the result, so a conviction is what is left after proof has won.
normal.cn: convict 是动作，conviction 是结果：证据赢了之后留下的东西就是定罪。

normal.en: The same word serves the courtroom and the heart.
normal.cn: 同一个词，既服务法庭，也服务人心。

normal.en: Say it with conviction and people lean in; say it without and they look away.
normal.cn: 带着信念说，人会靠近；不带信念说，人会转开目光。

normal.en: -ion turns the verb into a thing you can carry.
normal.cn: -ion 把动词变成一件可以带在身上的东西。

normal.en: A previous conviction is a past that keeps speaking in court.
normal.cn: 前科是一段在法庭上不断开口的过去。

abstract.en: Picture a stamped paper lying beside a closed hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张盖了章的纸，旁边是一只攥紧的手。

abstract.en: Picture a candle that stays lit in a windy room.
abstract.cn: 想象一支在风里也不灭的蜡烛。

abstract.en: Picture a root gripping stone and refusing to let go.
abstract.cn: 想象一条根抓住石头，怎么也不松开。

examples.en: He has two previous convictions for theft.
examples.cn: 他有两项盗窃前科。

examples.en: She argued her case with quiet conviction.
examples.cn: 她以平静而坚定的信念为自己的主张辩护。

examples.en: It is my conviction that small steps change a town.
examples.cn: 我深信小小的步伐能改变一座城镇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conviction 记成 convict（定罪）加 ion：法庭定下的罪，是定罪；心里定下的看法，是信念。

root: 源自拉丁语 convincere（用证据驳倒）的名词 convictio，由 com-（完全）与 vincere（征服）构成，本指证明有罪，后引申为坚定的信念。

sensesIntro.en: From a guilt proven in court, to a belief that proof cannot shake.
sensesIntro.cn: 从法庭上被证明的罪，到证据也摇不动的信念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a verdict sheet beside a tightly closed hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张判决书旁边，是一只攥紧的手。

branches.en: A court writes down what it has proved.
branches.cn: 法庭把已经证明的事写下来。

branches.en: A person holds fast to what argument cannot move.
branches.cn: 一个人紧紧抓住争辩也动不了的东西。

branches.en: Both are things settled beyond easy doubt.
branches.cn: 两者都是不容轻易动摇的定论。

branches.en: The legal sense is public, written and dated.
branches.cn: 法律义项是公开的、书面的、有日期的。

branches.en: The personal sense is quiet, inward and unrecorded.
branches.cn: 个人义项是安静的、向内的、不被记录的。

intro.en: Conviction is convict plus -ion, resting on Latin convincere, to overcome with proof.
intro.cn: conviction 是 convict 加 -ion，根源是拉丁语 convincere（用证据驳倒）。

latinIntro.en: The conquering base vict- or vinc- also runs through convince, victory and invincible.
latinIntro.cn: 征服词基 vict- 或 vinc- 也贯穿 convince、victory 与 invincible。

items.meaningCN: 已经定下的裁决或信念
items.example: The conviction stands.
items.exampleCN: 这项定罪成立。

items.example: They convicted the driver.
items.exampleCN: 他们判定司机有罪。

items.meaning: to win someone to a belief
items.meaningCN: 把某人争取到某种看法上
items.example: The data convinced us.
items.exampleCN: 数据说服了我们。

items.example: Her case was convincing.
items.exampleCN: 她的理由很有说服力。

items.example: The victor spoke briefly.
items.exampleCN: 胜者简短地讲了话。

items.example: It was a narrow victory.
items.exampleCN: 那是一场险胜。

items.example: The champion looked invincible.
items.exampleCN: 那位冠军看起来不可战胜。

items.example: The family was evicted.
items.exampleCN: 这家人被赶了出去。

definition_zh: 维护；保养；维持；维持费；生活费；扶养费；维修作业；维持性复述；维持期；装备维修保障
definition_en: the work of keeping equipment, buildings or systems in good condition; the act of keeping something in existence; or the money that supports a person
core_image: 一人一只手扶稳竖起的梯子，另一只手不停往齿轮上滴油
scene: 维修工扶着梯子给齿轮上油，日常的照料让设备继续运转。 One hand steadies the ladder while the other keeps oiling the gears: this everyday care is maintenance.
sceneCN: 这里 maintenance 是「日常保养」（第 1 个义项：设备保养）；句意：一只手扶稳梯子，另一只手不停给齿轮上油，这种日常照料就是保养。图中可辨识物件：人字梯、油壶、齿轮、油迹、工具箱；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 维护；保养；维持；生活费；扶养费；维修作业

collocations.zh: 维持期（治疗或体重管理）

forms.label: 单数（不可数，指保养工作）
复数（罕用，指多笔扶养费或多类维护）

senses.title: Routine upkeep: keeping equipment in working order
senses.titleCN: 日常保养：让设备一直能转
senses.definition: the regular work of cleaning, checking, adjusting and repairing equipment so that it keeps working
senses.definitionCN: 为让设备持续运转而定期进行的清洁、检查、调整与修理工作
senses.example: The aircraft is in the hangar for routine maintenance.
senses.exampleCN: 这架飞机正在机库里做日常保养。
senses.why: Old French maintenir meant to hold with the hand, and maintenance first named the act of holding something up. Applied to machines, that holding up becomes regular servicing: the thing is held in working order.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 maintenir 意为「用手握住」，maintenance 最初指把东西撑住这一行为。用在机器上，「撑住」就变成了定期保养：让它一直保持在可用状态。

senses.title: Keeping something in existence
senses.titleCN: 维持：使某物继续存在下去
senses.definition: the act of keeping something in existence or at the same level, so that it does not decay or disappear
senses.definitionCN: 使某物继续存在或保持在同一水平、不至于衰败或消失的行为
senses.example: The maintenance of peace required constant negotiation.
senses.exampleCN: 维持和平需要不断的谈判。
senses.why: The abstract sense comes straight from the literal one: to keep a thing in the hand is to keep it from falling away. What is held up here is a state, not a machine.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义直接从字面义来：把东西握在手里，就是不让它掉下去。这里被撑住的是某种状态，而不是机器。

senses.title: Money that supports a person: living costs, alimony
senses.titleCN: 生活费、扶养费：供养一个人的钱
senses.definition: money paid regularly to support a person's living costs, especially after a separation or divorce
senses.definitionCN: 定期支付以维持某人生活开支的钱，尤指分居或离婚之后的扶养费
senses.example: He pays monthly maintenance for his two children.
senses.exampleCN: 他每月为两个孩子支付扶养费。
senses.why: In law, maintenance was the support one person owed another. The image of holding someone up turns into money: what keeps a household standing is now paid in instalments.
senses.whyCN: 在法律中，maintenance 指一方对另一方应付的供养。把人「撑住」的意象转成了钱：让一个家庭不倒下的东西，如今按月支付。

senses.title: Public upkeep: roads, bridges and structures kept in repair
senses.titleCN: 公共设施养护：道路桥梁的修补
senses.definition: the work of keeping roads, bridges, railways and public structures in good repair
senses.definitionCN: 使道路、桥梁、铁路与公共建筑保持良好状态的养护工作
senses.example: Highway maintenance closes one lane every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 每年春天公路养护都会封闭一条车道。
senses.why: The thing held up is now a public structure rather than a private machine. English uses maintenance for the state's duty to keep shared surfaces usable.
senses.whyCN: 这里被撑住的是公共建筑，而不是私人机器。英语用 maintenance 指国家维持公共设施可用的职责。

senses.title: System maintenance: keeping software and data healthy
senses.titleCN: 系统维护：让软件与数据保持正常
senses.definition: the work of keeping software, servers, networks or databases in working order, often by planned updates
senses.definitionCN: 通过计划性更新等手段让软件、服务器、网络或数据库保持正常工作
senses.example: Scheduled maintenance will take the site offline for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 计划内维护会让网站离线一小时。
senses.why: Digital systems decay in their own way: patches fall behind, disks fill, certificates expire. The old word for holding a machine up was simply carried over to the invisible machinery.
senses.whyCN: 数字系统有自己的老化方式：补丁落后、磁盘写满、证书过期。原先用于撑住机器的旧词，直接搬到了这套看不见的机器上。

senses.title: Maintenance rehearsal: holding an item in memory
senses.titleCN: 维持性复述：把信息按原样留在记忆里
senses.definition: in psychology, repetition that keeps an item in memory without connecting it to other knowledge or moving it into long-term storage
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中指一种重复：只把信息留在记忆中，不与其它知识建立联系，也不转入长时记忆
senses.example: Repeating a phone number to yourself is maintenance rehearsal.
senses.exampleCN: 把电话号码反复默念，就是维持性复述。
senses.why: Here the thing held up is a memory trace. The word keeps its plain sense of holding, and the contrast is with elaborative rehearsal, which builds links instead of merely holding.
senses.whyCN: 这里被撑住的是一段记忆痕迹。词仍保留朴素的「撑住」义，与之相对的是精细复述——后者建立联系，而不只是撑住。

senses.title: Maintenance phase: holding a state instead of changing it
senses.titleCN: 维持期：不追求改变，只求稳住
senses.definition: a stage of treatment, weight control or training in which the present state is kept rather than improved
senses.definitionCN: 治疗、体重控制或训练中的一个阶段：保持现状而不继续改善
senses.example: After the diet, she entered a six-month maintenance phase.
senses.exampleCN: 节食结束后，她进入为期六个月的维持期。
senses.why: Medical language splits a course into an active phase and a holding phase. The second phase does exactly what the word says: it holds the gain already made.
senses.whyCN: 医学语言把疗程分为主动期与维持期。第二阶段做的正是字面所说的事：把已经取得的成果撑住。

senses.title: Equipment support in the military: keeping vehicles serviceable
senses.titleCN: 装备维修保障：让车辆武器随时可用
senses.definition: in military use, the logistics of keeping weapons, vehicles and equipment serviceable and supplied
senses.definitionCN: 军事用语中指使武器、车辆与装备保持可用并获得补给的勤务保障
senses.example: The unit's maintenance company repaired the trucks overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 该部队的维修连一夜之间修好了卡车。
senses.why: Armies turned upkeep into a named branch of logistics. The word covers repair, inspection, spare parts and recovery, all of it holding the force in a usable state.
senses.whyCN: 军队把保养变成后勤的一个专设分支。这个词涵盖修理、检查、备件与救援，全是把部队撑在可用状态。

intro.en: Maintenance came into English through Old French maintenance from the verb maintenir, which continues Latin manu tenere 'to hold with the hand'. That phrase is manus 'hand' plus tenere 'to hold'. The English noun first named the act of upholding something, then the money that upholds a household, and only later the servicing of machines. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: maintenance 经古法语 maintenance 进入英语，源自动词 maintenir，后者延续拉丁语 manu tenere「用手握住」，即 manus「手」加 tenere「握持」。英语名词最初指把东西撑住的行为，随后指撑起一个家庭的钱，最后才指机器的保养。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Maintenance becomes a standard engineering and computing term for planned upkeep, and maintenance-free enters product description.
items.cn: maintenance 成为工程与计算领域表示计划性保养的标准术语，maintenance-free 也进入产品说明。

items.en: Railways and factories give the word its modern weight: maintenance of rolling stock and machinery is a budgeted activity.
items.cn: 铁路与工厂赋予这个词现代的分量：机车与机械的维护成为要编预算的活动。

items.en: The legal sense 'support owed to a dependant' is recorded, turning upkeep into a regular payment.
items.cn: 「应付给受扶养人的生活费」这一法律义见于记载，把保养变成了定期付款。

items.en: English maintenance is recorded in the sense of upholding or defending something, borrowed from Old French.
items.cn: 英语 maintenance 见于记载，义为撑住或维护某物，借自古法语。

items.en: manu tenere 'to hold with the hand' is the source phrase; tenere also gives tenant, tenable, retain, contain and sustain.
items.cn: manu tenere「用手握住」是源头词组；tenere 还给出 tenant、tenable、retain、contain、sustain。

note.en: The first group separates the real family from words that only resemble it or are misspelled; the second compares near synonyms that each cover part of maintenance.
note.cn: 第一组把真正的同族词与只是形似或拼错的词分开；第二组比较近义词，它们各自覆盖 maintenance 的一部分。

entries.definition: a person or thing that holds a group together, or the rope that supports a ship's mainmast. It is main 'chief' plus stay, a nautical term, not manus plus tenere.
entries.definitionCN: 维系一个群体的主要人物或事物，或指支撑主桅的绳索。它是 main「主要的」加航海词 stay「支索」，而不是 manus 加 tenere。

entries.definition: to keep something in good condition, to keep it in existence, or to assert something firmly. It is the verb behind maintenance and keeps all three threads.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物保持良好状态、使某物继续存在，或坚定主张某事。它是 maintenance 背后的动词，三条语义线都保留着。

entries.definition: A common misspelling of maintenance, which follows the French stem mainten- rather than the English verb maintain. There is no such standard spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 这是 maintenance 的常见拼错形式；正确拼写沿用法语词干 mainten-，而不是英语动词 maintain 的词形。并不存在这一标准拼法。

entries.definition: the everyday care and cost of keeping property or equipment in condition. It leans toward the money and effort spent rather than the technical work.
entries.definitionCN: 让房产或设备保持状态的日常照料及其花费。它偏向所花的钱和精力，而不是技术性的维修工作。

entries.definition: the scheduled technical attention given to a machine, such as oil changes and inspections. It is the concrete task, where maintenance is the whole programme.
entries.definitionCN: 给机器定期做的技术性照料，如换油和检查。它是具体的一项活，而 maintenance 是整套安排。

entries.definition: the court-ordered payment to a former spouse. It is the legal name for one kind of maintenance, from Latin alimonia 'nourishment', not a general term for upkeep.
entries.definitionCN: 法院判决支付给前配偶的钱。它是 maintenance 中一种的法律名称，出自拉丁语 alimonia「滋养」，不是保养的统称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pieces of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: manu tenere is 'hold with the hand'; maintenance is the act of holding something up so it does not fall.
normal.cn: manu tenere 是「用手握住」；maintenance 就是把东西撑住、不让它倒下的行为。

normal.en: The noun keeps the French stem mainten-, which is why it is spelled maintenance and not maintainance.
normal.cn: 这个名词保留了法语词干 mainten-，所以拼作 maintenance 而不是 maintainance。

normal.en: tenere, the 'hold' half, also gives tenant, tenable, retain, contain and sustain: every one of them is holding something.
normal.cn: 表示「握持」的 tenere 还给出 tenant、tenable、retain、contain、sustain，每一个都含有「握持」。

normal.en: The same noun covers a machine, a peace, a child and a data centre, because all of them can fall down if nobody holds them up.
normal.cn: 同一个名词既能指机器、和平、孩子，也能指数据中心，因为只要无人撑住，它们都会倒。

normal.en: maintenance-free is the exact negation: no holding up is needed.
normal.cn: maintenance-free 正是它的反义：不需要任何撑住。

abstract.en: Picture a hand under a leaning ladder: maintenance is that hand, whether the ladder is a bus, a marriage or a database.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手托住倾斜的梯子：maintenance 就是那只手，无论梯子是公交车、婚姻还是数据库。

abstract.en: See upkeep as a steady drip of small acts; stop dripping and the machine, the peace or the gain begins to fail.
abstract.cn: 把保养看成一滴一滴的小动作；一旦停止滴油，机器、和平或成果就开始衰败。

abstract.en: The word never means improvement: it means holding the present state, which is why a maintenance phase follows the active one.
abstract.cn: 这个词从不表示改善：它表示把现状撑住，所以主动期之后才有维持期。

examples.en: Poor maintenance is a more common cause of failure than worn parts.
examples.cn: 保养不善比零件磨损更常导致故障。

examples.en: The foundation pays maintenance to the families of injured workers.
examples.cn: 该基金会向受伤工人的家庭支付扶养费。

examples.en: Regular maintenance of the trails keeps hikers safe.
examples.cn: 定期维护步道能保障徒步者的安全。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「门特嫩死」——门轴得常抹油，不然就卡死 → maintenance 维护、保养

root: 拉丁语 manu tenere「用手握住」＝manus「手」＋tenere「握持」，经古法语 maintenir、maintenance 进入英语。核心是「一直用手撑住，不让它倒下」：撑住机器是保养，撑住生活是扶养费，撑住状态是维持。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: a hand holding something up. What changes is what is held: a machine, a peace, a household, a road, a server, a memory, a treatment result, or an army's vehicles.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：一只手把东西撑住。变化的只是撑住的是什么：机器、和平、家庭、道路、服务器、记忆、治疗成果，还是一支军队的车辆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand steadying a ladder while the other oils the gears.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手扶稳梯子，另一只手给齿轮上油。

branches.en: HOLDING UP: the physical hand becomes routine servicing for a machine, and simple keeping for a state of affairs.
branches.cn: 撑住：有形的手变成对机器的定期保养，对事态则变成单纯的维持。

branches.en: MONEY AS SUPPORT: what holds a household up is paid regularly, and law names it maintenance.
branches.cn: 以钱撑住：撑起一个家庭的东西按月支付，法律称之为扶养费。

branches.en: SHARED AND DIGITAL SURFACES: roads and servers are held usable for everyone who depends on them.
branches.cn: 公共与数字设施：道路与服务器为所有依赖它们的人保持在可用状态。

branches.en: HOLDING A STATE: a memory trace or a treatment gain is kept exactly as it is, without further change.
branches.cn: 撑住状态：记忆痕迹或治疗成果被原样保持，不再进一步改变。

branches.en: HOLDING A FORCE: military logistics keeps vehicles and weapons serviceable so the unit can act.
branches.cn: 撑住武力：军事后勤让车辆与武器保持可用，使部队能够行动。

intro.en: Maintenance is Latin manu tenere 'to hold with the hand' plus the French noun ending -ance, from Latin -antia. The ending turns the act of holding into the name of that act.
intro.cn: maintenance 是拉丁语 manu tenere「用手握住」加法语名词词尾 -ance（出自拉丁 -antia）。这个词尾把「握持」这一动作变成该动作的名称。

latinIntro.en: The two Latin pieces are manus 'hand' and tenere 'to hold'. tenere supplies the stems ten- and -tain, visible in tenant, tenable, retain, contain, sustain and maintain.
latinIntro.cn: 两个拉丁成分是 manus「手」与 tenere「握持」。tenere 提供 ten- 与 -tain 词干，见于 tenant、tenable、retain、contain、sustain、maintain。

items.meaning: the act of keeping something up
items.meaningCN: 维持、保养的行为（-ance 构成动作名词）
items.example: Routine maintenance keeps the pumps running.
items.exampleCN: 日常保养让水泵持续运转。

items.meaning: to keep in condition, keep in being, or assert
items.example: They maintain the bridge every summer.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年夏天维护这座桥。

items.meaning: able to be kept up or defended
items.example: The design is simple and easily maintainable.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计简单，易于维护。

items.meaning: the ease with which something can be kept in service
items.meaningCN: 可维护性；便于保养的程度
items.example: Engineers tested the maintainability of the new engine.
items.exampleCN: 工程师测试了新发动机的可维护性。

items.meaning: a person or tool that keeps something in order
items.meaningCN: 维护者；保养人员或工具
items.example: The software has only one active maintainer.
items.exampleCN: 这款软件只有一名在任维护者。

items.meaning: one who holds a rented property
items.meaningCN: 承租人；房客（字面「持有者」）
items.example: The tenant renewed the lease for a year.
items.exampleCN: 房客续签了一年租约。

items.meaning: able to be held or defended against objection
items.example: That argument is no longer tenable.
items.exampleCN: 那个论点已经站不住脚了。

items.meaning: to keep or hold on to something
items.meaningCN: 保留；保持（re- 表示向后）
items.example: The soil retains water after rain.
items.exampleCN: 雨后土壤能保住水分。

items.meaning: to hold inside, or to keep within limits
items.meaningCN: 容纳；控制住（con- 表示合在一起）
items.example: The box contains old letters.
items.exampleCN: 这个盒子里装着旧信件。

items.meaning: to hold up from beneath, and so to keep going
items.meaningCN: 支撑；使持续（sus- 表示从下方）
items.example: The soil sustains a dense forest.
items.exampleCN: 这片土壤养着茂密的森林。

latinEntries.meaning: to hold with the hand, hence to keep up
latinEntries.meaningCN: 用手握住，因而引申为维持

latinEntries.meaning: forms an abstract noun of action, French -ance
latinEntries.meaningCN: 构成动作抽象名词，法语作 -ance

definition_zh: 含糊的；模糊的；不明确的；隐约的
definition_en: not expressed or understood clearly, or seen only in an unclear outline
core_image: 隔着一层蒙雾的玻璃看外面走过来的人
scene: 雾很重，街对面有人在挥手，轮廓却像是被水泡开了一样，看不清到底是谁。 His answer was so vague that nobody knew the date.
sceneCN: 这里 vague 是「含糊的、不明确的」（第 1 个义项：说法不清楚）；句意为他的回答太含糊，谁也没弄明白日期。隔着蒙雾看人的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「模糊地；含糊地」
加 -ness 构成名词，义为「含糊；模糊」
同根名词，义为「奇想；无常的变化」
同根动词，义为「离题；漫游」

senses.title: Not clearly stated
senses.definition: expressed in words that leave the meaning unclear
senses.definitionCN: 用让人无法确定含义的话表达
senses.example: The letter was vague about the exact time.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信对具体时间说得很含糊。
senses.why: A word that means wandering cannot pin anything down, so speech built on it leaves the listener without a fixed point.
senses.whyCN: 一个意为「游走」的词抓不住任何东西，因此由它构成的言语让听的人找不到落点。

senses.title: Without a clear shape
senses.definition: seen or remembered without clear outlines
senses.definitionCN: 看到或记得的东西轮廓不清
senses.example: A vague shape moved behind the curtain.
senses.exampleCN: 窗帘后面有个模糊的影子在动。
senses.why: An outline that will not settle is a wandering line, which is exactly what the Latin adjective describes.
senses.whyCN: 定不下来的轮廓就是一条游走的线，这正是那个拉丁形容词所描述的。

senses.title: An idea not fully formed
senses.definition: of a thought or feeling that is not yet worked out
senses.definitionCN: 形容想法或感觉尚未成形
senses.example: I had only a vague idea of what the job involved.
senses.exampleCN: 我对这份工作具体干什么只有个模糊的概念。
senses.why: Thoughts take shape gradually, and while the shape wanders it can only be described as unclear.
senses.whyCN: 想法是慢慢成形的，形状还在游走时，就只能说它不明确。

senses.title: Uncertain or absent-minded
senses.definition: of a person, not paying full attention or not sure of things
senses.definitionCN: 形容人不专注或对事情没把握
senses.example: She looked vaguely at the papers and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 她心不在焉地看了看那些文件，什么也没说。
senses.why: A mind that wanders off has no fixed object of attention, so the same adjective describes the person.
senses.whyCN: 心思走神的人没有固定的注意对象，于是同一个形容词也用来说人。

intro.en: A Latin adjective of wandering borrowed through French, with no live prefix or suffix inside it.
intro.cn: 一个意为「漫游」的拉丁形容词经法语借入，里面已没有仍在起作用的前后缀。

items.en: Vagus meant wandering, unsettled, or uncertain, and vagari meant to roam about.
items.cn: vagus 意为「漫游的、不定的、含糊的」，vagari 意为「四处游荡」。

items.en: The word entered French as vague, where the hard g softened before the final vowel.
items.cn: 这个词以 vague 的形式进入法语，尾元音前的 g 也随之软化。

items.en: English adopts the word in the sixteenth century for unclear statements.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪采用这个词，指不清楚的说法。

items.en: The sense extends to outlines and memories that cannot be fixed.
items.cn: 词义扩展到无法定形的轮廓与记忆上。

items.en: Vaguely and vagueness become the common adverb and noun of the family.
items.cn: vaguely 与 vagueness 成为这一词族常用的副词与名词。

note.en: The look-alike group is the small vag- family, and the near-meaning group pairs unclear with plain and certain.
note.cn: 形近组是小小的 vag- 词族，近义组把模糊与清楚、确定相对照。

entries.definition: in an unclear way
entries.definitionCN: 模糊地；含糊地

entries.definition: lack of clarity
entries.definitionCN: 含糊；模糊

entries.definition: a wandering, unpredictable notion
entries.definitionCN: 奇想；无常的变化

entries.definition: the current fashion, only the spelling looks close, the root is different
entries.definitionCN: 风尚；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: not easy to understand
entries.definitionCN: 不清楚的

entries.definition: open to more than one meaning
entries.definitionCN: 模棱两可的

entries.definition: blurred and hard to make out
entries.definitionCN: 不清晰的

entries.definition: exact and clear
entries.definitionCN: 精确的

normalIntro.en: Hold on to wandering: a line that wanders has no clear edge, and neither does a vague answer.
normalIntro.cn: 抓住「游走」这个意思：游走的线没有清楚的边，含糊的回答也一样。

normal.en: Vague about something is the standard frame for being unclear.
normal.cn: vague about something 是表示「说不清」的标准框架。

normal.en: The adverb vaguely often means slightly, as in vaguely familiar.
normal.cn: 副词 vaguely 常表示「略微」，如 vaguely familiar。

normal.en: Vagueness is criticised in academic writing, where precision is expected.
normal.cn: 学术写作要求精确，所以常批评 vagueness。

normal.en: The comparative is vaguer, keeping the e in spelling.
normal.cn: 比较级是 vaguer，拼写里保留了 e。

normal.en: The same root appears in vagary, a wandering notion.
normal.cn: 同一词根见于 vagary，指游移不定的念头。

abstract.en: Picture a person waving across a street through heavy fog.
abstract.cn: 想象雾中街对面一个人在挥手。

abstract.en: Hear an instruction that says soon, without any hour.
abstract.cn: 听一句只说要「很快」却没有钟点的指示。

abstract.en: Try to recall a face from a dream and lose the eyes.
abstract.cn: 试着回忆梦里的一张脸，眼睛却总是想不起来。

examples.en: He was vague about where he had been that night.
examples.cn: 他对那晚去了哪里说得含含糊糊。

examples.en: I have only a vague memory of the house.
examples.cn: 我对那栋房子只有模糊的记忆。

examples.en: She waved vaguely toward the door and left.
examples.cn: 她心不在焉地朝门口挥了挥手就走了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「微格」——答案只剩微博那么一格，自然含含糊糊。

root: 拉丁语 vagus（漫游的、不定的）与 vagari（游荡），经法语 vague 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: Wandering yields lines that will not settle, and those lines give unclear speech, blurred outlines, unfinished ideas, and a mind that drifts.
sensesIntro.cn: 「漫游」带来定不下来的线条，而这些线条给出含糊的言语、模糊的轮廓、未完形的想法与飘走的注意力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure waving through a misted window.
core.cn: 核心意象：隔着蒙雾的玻璃，一个人影在挥手。

branches.en: The words branch: an answer that will not commit.
branches.cn: 言辞分支：不肯明确的回答。

branches.en: The shape branch: a silhouette without an outline.
branches.cn: 轮廓分支：没有清晰边界的身影。

branches.en: The idea branch: a notion still without edges.
branches.cn: 念头分支：还没有边界的想法。

branches.en: The person branch: eyes that are not quite here.
branches.cn: 人身分支：眼神并不完全在此处。

branches.en: The clarity branch: what is missing is the plain outline of things.
branches.cn: 清晰分支：缺的正是事物清楚的样子。

intro.en: A borrowed adjective with no live prefix; its only everyday additions are -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: 一个借入的形容词，没有仍起作用的前缀；日常只在其后加 -ly 与 -ness。

latinIntro.en: Latin vagus, wandering, plus the verb vagari, to roam, share one root with no surviving prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vagus（漫游的）与动词 vagari（游荡）共用一个词根，没有留存下来的前缀。

items.example: A wandering line never settles.
items.exampleCN: 游走的线条总定不下来。

items.example: French gave the word its softer ending.
items.exampleCN: 法语给了这个词更柔和的词尾。

items.example: Vaguely describes an unclear way.
items.exampleCN: vaguely 描述不明确的方式。

items.example: Vagueness is the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: vagueness 就是这一性质本身。

items.example: Vagary is a wandering fancy.
items.exampleCN: vagary 是游移的念头。

items.example: Divagate adds the idea of straying away.
items.exampleCN: divagate 加上「偏离」的意思。

items.example: Clear answers leave no doubt.
items.exampleCN: 清楚的回答不留疑问。

items.example: A blur is what vague things look like.
items.exampleCN: 模糊之物看起来就是一团晕影。

definition_zh: 伤害；损害；危害
definition_en: damage or injury to a person or thing, or to cause such damage
core_image: 一只脚踩坏了刚刚长出的嫩芽
scene: 吸烟会伤害身体。 Smoking can harm your health.
sceneCN: 这里 harm 是「伤害」（第 3 个义项，动词）；句意：吸烟会伤害身体。

senses.title: Injury to the body
senses.definition: physical injury or damage to a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 对人畜造成的身体损伤
senses.example: The fall did him no harm.
senses.exampleCN: 那一跤没有伤到他。
senses.why: This is the basic injury sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的损伤义项。

senses.title: Damage to interests
senses.definition: damage to something valuable, such as trust or reputation
senses.definitionCN: 对信任、名誉等有价值之物的破坏
senses.example: The rumour harmed her reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 那则谣言损害了她的名誉。
senses.why: What can hurt a body can hurt a name.
senses.whyCN: 能伤身体的，也能伤名声。

senses.title: Cause damage
senses.definition: to cause damage or injury to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物造成损伤或破坏
senses.example: Smoking can harm your health.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟会伤害身体。
senses.why: The noun of damage became a verb.
senses.whyCN: 损害的名词，转成了动词。

intro.en: Harm comes from Old English hearm, injury or grief.
intro.cn: harm 来自古英语 hearm，意为伤害或悲痛。

items.en: The root meant injury.
items.cn: 该词根意为损伤。

items.en: Hearm meant harm or sorrow.
items.cn: hearm 意为伤害或悲伤。

items.en: Harm named damage of any kind.
items.cn: harm 指任何形式的损害。

items.en: The verb sense of injuring grew.
items.cn: 「使受伤」的动词义发展起来。

items.en: The phrase no harm done became common.
items.cn: no harm done 成为常用说法。

note.en: Harm is compared with look-alike words and with words for damage and injury.
note.cn: 把 harm 与形近词以及表示损害和伤害的词作比较。

entries.definition: firm or difficult
entries.definitionCN: 硬的；困难的

entries.definition: an animal like a rabbit
entries.definitionCN: 野兔

entries.definition: a stringed instrument
entries.definitionCN: 竖琴

entries.definition: harm done to a thing
entries.definitionCN: 损坏

entries.definition: harm done to a body
entries.definitionCN: 受伤

entries.definition: to cause pain
entries.definitionCN: 使疼痛

normalIntro.en: Harm is a foot on a young shoot, a word on a good name, and an action against a body.
normalIntro.cn: harm 是踩在新芽上的一只脚，是落在好名声上的一句话，也是加在身体上的一个动作。

normal.en: Too much sugar can harm your teeth.
normal.cn: 吃糖太多会损害牙齿。

normal.en: The storm did little harm.
normal.cn: 风暴造成的损害不大。

normal.en: No harm done, so let us go on.
normal.cn: 没造成伤害，我们继续吧。

normal.en: The law protects animals from harm.
normal.cn: 法律保护动物免受伤害。

normal.en: He meant no harm.
normal.cn: 他并没有恶意。

abstract.en: What is done in a moment can harm for years.
abstract.cn: 一瞬间做的事，能伤害很多年。

abstract.en: The softest words can leave the deepest marks.
abstract.cn: 最软的话，能留下最深的痕。

abstract.en: To mean no harm is not the same as doing none.
abstract.cn: 没有恶意，不等于没有伤害。

examples.en: Smoking can harm your health.
examples.cn: 吸烟会伤害身体。

examples.en: The rumour harmed her reputation.
examples.cn: 那则谣言损害了她的名誉。

examples.en: The fall did him no harm.
examples.cn: 那一跤没有伤到他。

dict_mnemonic.text: harm 可作名词也可作动词，都是「伤害、损害」；do harm to 是对……有害，no harm done 是没造成伤害，harm the environment 是损害环境。

root: 来自古英语 hearm（伤害、悲伤），源于日耳曼语；由身体的损伤，引申为名誉、利益与环境所受的破坏。

sensesIntro.en: Harm is injury to a body, damage to something valued, or the act of causing either.
sensesIntro.cn: harm 是对身体的损伤、对有价值之物的破坏，或造成这两者的行为。

core.en: A blow that leaves a mark.
core.cn: 留下痕迹的一击。

branches.en: A knee hits stone and swells.
branches.cn: 膝盖撞上石头，肿了起来。

branches.en: A false story spreads through a town.
branches.cn: 一个假消息在小镇传开。

branches.en: Smoke enters a pair of lungs.
branches.cn: 烟雾进入双肺。

branches.en: An injury and an injuring act are one event.
branches.cn: 伤与致伤的动作，是同一件事。

branches.en: A body and a reputation bruise the same way.
branches.cn: 身体与名誉，受伤的方式一样。

intro.en: Harm takes verb endings and forms two contrasting adjectives with -ful and -less.
intro.cn: harm 加动词词尾，并用 -ful 与 -less 构成两个相对形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: The harm was small.
items.exampleCN: 伤害不大。

items.example: Noise harms hearing.
items.exampleCN: 噪音损害听力。

items.example: No one was harmed.
items.exampleCN: 没有人受伤。

items.example: He is harming himself.
items.exampleCN: 他在伤害自己。

items.example: It is a harmful habit.
items.exampleCN: 这是个有害的习惯。

items.example: The insect is harmless.
items.exampleCN: 这种昆虫无害。

items.example: The waste was disposed of harmfully.
items.exampleCN: 这些废物被有害地处理了。

items.example: No harm done, so relax.
items.exampleCN: 没事，放松些。

definition_zh: 使暴露；揭露；使接触
definition_en: to leave something open to danger or influence; to reveal a truth; to give someone experience of something
core_image: 遮布被掀开，里面的东西露在光下
scene: 不要把皮肤长时间暴露在阳光下。 Do not expose your skin to the sun for long.
sceneCN: 这里 expose 是「使暴露于」（第 1 个义项）；句意：不要把皮肤长时间暴露在阳光下。

senses.title: Leave open to harm
senses.definition: to leave someone or something open to danger, weather, or influence
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物处于危险、天气或影响之下
senses.example: The damaged roof exposed the room to rain.
senses.exampleCN: 损坏的屋顶让雨水淋进了房间。
senses.why: The core sense is removing cover or protection.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是去掉遮盖或保护。

senses.title: Reveal a truth
senses.definition: to make a secret or wrong doing public
senses.definitionCN: 把秘密或错误行为公开
senses.example: The report exposed serious waste.
senses.exampleCN: 报告揭露了严重的浪费。
senses.why: Physical uncovering becomes moral disclosure.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的揭开转为道德上的揭发。

senses.title: Give experience
senses.definition: to give someone experience of something new
senses.definitionCN: 让某人接触或体验新事物
senses.example: Travel exposes children to other cultures.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行让孩子们接触其他文化。
senses.why: Being open to influence becomes learning.
senses.whyCN: 向影响敞开变成学习的过程。

intro.en: Expose comes from Latin exponere, to put out, from ex- out and ponere to place.
intro.cn: expose 来自拉丁语 exponere（放出去），由 ex-（向外）与 ponere（放置）构成。

items.en: Ex- means out.
items.cn: ex- 意为向外。

items.en: Ponere means to place.
items.cn: ponere 意为放置。

items.en: Exponere means to put out or set forth.
items.cn: exponere 意为放出或陈述。

items.en: Exposer carries the sense of setting out.
items.cn: 古法语 exposer 保留「摆出来」之义。

items.en: Expose means to uncover or reveal.
items.cn: 现代英语中 expose 意为使暴露或揭露。

note.en: Expose means uncover; oppose means stand against.
note.cn: expose 是揭开，oppose 则是反对。

entries.definition: to disagree with and try to stop
entries.definitionCN: 反对

entries.definition: to think something is likely
entries.definitionCN: 假设；认为

entries.definition: to get rid of something
entries.definitionCN: 处理；丢弃

entries.definition: to make something known
entries.definitionCN: 揭示

entries.definition: to remove a cover or find a secret
entries.definitionCN: 揭开；发现

entries.definition: to show something openly
entries.definitionCN: 展示

normalIntro.en: Expose is about taking away cover, whether from skin or from a secret.
normalIntro.cn: expose 指去掉遮盖，无论是皮肤上的还是秘密上的。

normal.en: Do not expose the film to bright light.
normal.cn: 不要让胶片暴露在强光下。

normal.en: The newspaper exposed the false claims.
normal.cn: 报纸揭露了那些虚假说法。

normal.en: Workers were exposed to dangerous fumes.
normal.cn: 工人们接触到了危险气体。

normal.en: The scandal exposed weak controls.
normal.cn: 这起丑闻暴露出监管薄弱。

normal.en: Good teachers expose students to new ideas.
normal.cn: 好老师让学生接触新思想。

abstract.en: Picture a cloth pulled away from a hidden object.
abstract.cn: 想象一块布从隐藏的物体上被拉开。

abstract.en: Imagine a spotlight falling on a dark corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一束聚光灯照进黑暗的角落。

abstract.en: Think of a door opened to let fresh air in.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门打开，让新鲜空气进来。

examples.en: The report exposed waste in the department.
examples.cn: 报告揭露了该部门的浪费。

examples.en: Children should not be exposed to violence.
examples.cn: 不应让儿童接触暴力。

examples.en: The storm exposed the weakness of the roof.
examples.cn: 暴风雨暴露了屋顶的弱点。

dict_mnemonic.text: ex（向外）加 pose（放置）：把东西放到外面、不再遮住，就是 expose（暴露）。

root: 源自拉丁语 exponere（放出去），由 ex-（向外）与 ponere（放置）构成，核心义「去掉遮盖，使显露」。

sensesIntro.en: Expose means to leave something unprotected, to reveal a truth, or to give someone new experience.
sensesIntro.cn: expose 意为使失去保护、揭露真相，或让某人获得新体验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cover lifted off something hidden.
core.cn: 核心意象：遮盖物被从隐藏之物上掀开。

branches.en: The base sense is opening to harm.
branches.cn: 基础义是向伤害敞开。

branches.en: Physical uncovering becomes public disclosure.
branches.cn: 物理上的揭开变成公开揭露。

branches.en: Being open to influence becomes learning.
branches.cn: 向影响敞开变成学习。

branches.en: A hidden fault can be exposed to view.
branches.cn: 隐藏的缺陷可以被暴露在眼前。

branches.en: Exposure to risk and exposure to new ideas share the same openness.
branches.cn: 暴露于风险与接触新思想都带有「敞开」之意。

intro.en: Expose belongs to the Latin ponere family, like expose and composition.
intro.cn: expose 属于拉丁语 ponere 词族，与 composition 等词同源。

latinIntro.en: Latin exponere, ponere, and the prefix ex- are the source elements.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exponere、ponere 与前缀 ex- 是来源要素。

items.example: They exposed the faulty wiring.
items.exampleCN: 他们揭露了有问题的线路。

items.example: The test exposes weak spots.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试暴露出薄弱之处。

items.example: The exposed pipe froze in winter.
items.exampleCN: 暴露的管道冬天冻住了。

items.example: Exposing fraud takes courage.
items.exampleCN: 揭露欺诈需要勇气。

items.example: Exposure to cold can be dangerous.
items.exampleCN: 受寒可能很危险。

items.meaning: a full explanation or public show
items.example: The book begins with a short exposition.
items.exampleCN: 这本书以简短的阐述开篇。

items.example: The material is exposable to sunlight.
items.exampleCN: 这种材料可以暴露在阳光下。

items.example: Many residents oppose the plan.
items.exampleCN: 许多居民反对这个计划。

items.meaning: to place an idea before oneself
items.example: I suppose he will arrive soon.
items.exampleCN: 我想他很快就会到。

latinEntries.meaning: to put out or set forth

definition_zh: 发动机；引擎；火车头；推动力
definition_en: a machine that converts power into motion, or something that drives a process
core_image: 发动机低低地震动，把整辆车推向前方
scene: 汽车发动机发出低低的响声。 The car engine made a low sound.
sceneCN: 这里 engine 是「发动机」（第 1 个义项：把动力转化为运动的机器）；句意：汽车发动机发出低低的响声。

pos.zh: 发动机；引擎；火车头；推动力

senses.title: A machine that produces motion
senses.definition: a machine that turns fuel or electricity into movement
senses.definitionCN: 把燃料或电力转化为运动的机器
senses.example: The car engine made a low sound.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车发动机发出低低的响声。
senses.why: The word descends from a term for skill or invention, so the machine is a product of clever design.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自表示技巧或发明的词，因此机器是巧妙设计的产物。

senses.title: A railway locomotive
senses.definition: the part of a train that provides the power to pull it
senses.definitionCN: 火车中提供牵引动力的部分
senses.example: The engine pulled ten carriages.
senses.exampleCN: 火车头拉动了十节车厢。
senses.why: Early locomotives were the most visible engines, so the word became their everyday name.
senses.whyCN: 早期机车是最显眼的发动机，因此这个词成了它们的日常名称。

senses.title: A force that drives a process
senses.definition: something that causes or drives activity, growth, or change
senses.definitionCN: 引起或推动活动、成长或变化的事物
senses.example: Trade is the engine of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易是这座城市的推动力。
senses.why: A machine's engine moves a vehicle, so the image transfers to anything that drives progress.
senses.whyCN: 机器的发动机推动车辆，因此这一意象转移到任何推动进步的事物上。

intro.en: Engine comes from Latin ingenium, natural ability or clever invention.
intro.cn: engine 来自拉丁语 ingenium，意为天赋或巧妙的发明。

items.en: Ingenium means inborn talent or cleverness.
items.cn: ingenium 意为天赋或聪明才智。

items.en: Engin means skill, a device, or a war machine.
items.cn: engin 意为技巧、装置或攻城器械。

items.en: English borrows engine for a device or invention.
items.cn: 英语借入 engine，指装置或发明。

items.en: Steam engines make the machine sense dominant.
items.cn: 蒸汽机让机器义成为主要含义。

items.en: Engine means a motor, a locomotive, or a driving force.
items.cn: 现代英语中，engine 指发动机、机车或推动力。

note.en: An engine converts power into motion; a motor is often electric, and a machine is the broader word.
note.cn: engine 把动力转化为运动，motor 常指电动机，machine 是更宽泛的词。

entries.definition: a person who designs machines or structures
entries.definitionCN: 工程师

entries.definition: the work of designing machines and structures
entries.definitionCN: 工程学；工程设计

entries.definition: more than one engine
entries.definitionCN: engine 的复数

entries.definition: a machine that produces movement, often electric
entries.definitionCN: 电动机；马达

entries.definition: a device with moving parts that does work
entries.definitionCN: 机器

entries.definition: a railway engine
entries.definitionCN: 机车；火车头

normalIntro.en: An engine is a clever machine that turns power into motion.
normalIntro.cn: engine 是把动力变成运动的巧妙机器。

normal.en: The car engine started.
normal.cn: 汽车发动机启动了。

normal.en: A steam engine pulled the train.
normal.cn: 蒸汽机拉动火车。

normal.en: The engine room is below deck.
normal.cn: 发动机舱在甲板下。

normal.en: Trade is the engine of growth.
normal.cn: 贸易是增长的引擎。

normal.en: Engineering designs engines.
normal.cn: 工程学设计发动机。

abstract.en: Picture pistons rising and falling in rhythm.
abstract.cn: 想象活塞有节奏地上下运动。

abstract.en: See a locomotive breathing steam.
abstract.cn: 想象机车喷出蒸汽。

abstract.en: Think of a hidden force pushing everything forward.
abstract.cn: 想象隐藏的力量推动一切向前。

examples.en: The car engine made a low sound.
examples.cn: 汽车发动机发出低低的响声。

examples.en: The engine pulled ten carriages.
examples.cn: 火车头拉动了十节车厢。

examples.en: Trade is the engine of the city.
examples.cn: 贸易是这座城市的推动力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「恩斤」——机器吃进燃料、使出力气；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ingenium（天赋、巧妙发明），经古法语 engin 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers motors, railway locomotives, and any force that drives progress.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖发动机、铁路机车，以及任何推动进步的力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pistons turning fuel into steady motion.
core.cn: 核心意象：活塞把燃料变成稳定运动。

branches.en: The base sense is a machine that makes motion.
branches.cn: 基本义是产生运动的机器。

branches.en: The railway locomotive is the classic engine.

definition_zh: 出现；露面；外表；外观；登场；到场
definition_en: the act of coming into sight or being present; the way someone or something looks
core_image: 一个人从幕后走到灯下，也带着此刻的样子
scene: 剧院后台的门被推开，化妆师最后看了一眼镜中的演员。 Her appearance on stage was greeted with a long round of applause.
sceneCN: 这里 appearance 是「登场；露面」（第 1 个义项：出现在人们眼前这一行为）；句意为「她在台上的登场赢得了一长阵掌声」。画面里有剧院后台的门、镜中的演员和化妆师。

pos.zh: 名词：出现；露面；外表；外观；登场；到场

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀 -ance 得到的动词，义为「出现；显得」
与 appearance 同出拉丁语 apparere，义为「明显的；表面上的」
由 apparent 加 -ly 构成，义为「看来；据说」
由同一拉丁词根派生，义为「幽灵；幻影」

senses.title: The act of appearing
senses.definition: the act of coming into sight or being present before people
senses.definitionCN: 进入视野或出现在人们面前这一行为
senses.example: Her appearance on stage was greeted with a long round of applause.
senses.exampleCN: 她在台上的登场赢得了一长阵掌声。
senses.why: The noun names the event of the Latin verb: a figure that was behind the curtain now stands where everyone can see it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名那个拉丁动词的事件：原本在幕后的身影，如今站在人人看得见的地方。

senses.title: The outward look
senses.definition: the way a person or thing looks to others, especially on the outside
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或一件东西呈现给别人的样子，尤指外在的样子
senses.example: The building has changed little in appearance.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼在外观上几乎没有变化。
senses.why: What appears is also what is judged, so the event of appearing turns into the permanent surface by which things are recognized.
senses.whyCN: 显现出来的东西也正是被评判的东西，于是「出现」这一事件转成事物借以被认出的持久表面。

senses.title: A public or formal presence
senses.definition: a single act of attending or being seen in public, often noted by others
senses.definitionCN: 一次出席或在公众面前被看见的行为，常被别人注意到
senses.example: He made a brief appearance at the reception.
senses.exampleCN: 他在招待会上短暂露了一面。
senses.why: Public life counts appearances: being seen once at the right place can carry as much weight as a whole speech.
senses.whyCN: 公共生活要算计「露面」：在合适的场合被看见一次，分量可能抵得上一整篇讲话。

senses.title: A performance or published work
senses.definition: an occasion of performing, or the publication and arrival of a work before the public
senses.definitionCN: 一次演出的场合，或一部作品出版并来到公众面前的时刻
senses.example: The appearance of her first novel surprised the critics.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一部小说的问世让评论家们吃了一惊。
senses.why: A book appears in the world as an actor appears on stage: both cross from obscurity into the public eye.
senses.whyCN: 一本书在世界中「出现」，正如演员在舞台上「出现」：两者都是从默默无闻跨入公众视野。

senses.title: Outward impression, as opposed to fact
senses.definition: in phrases such as to all appearances, the impression given, which may differ from the truth
senses.definitionCN: 用于 to all appearances 一类短语，指给出的印象，可能与事实不符
senses.example: To all appearances, the two firms were still friendly rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 从表面上看，这两家公司仍是友好的竞争对手。
senses.why: Since appearance is only the surface, the noun can also warn that the surface is not the whole story.
senses.whyCN: 既然 appearance 只是表面，这个名词也能提醒：表面并不等于全部实情。

intro.en: Appearance is the noun built on appear, and it inherits the Latin idea of 'coming into view'.
intro.cn: appearance 是建立在 appear 之上的名词，继承了拉丁语「进入视野」的观念。

items.en: Apparere 'come into view' is the verb behind the whole family, built from ad- 'to' and parere 'come forth'.
items.cn: apparere「进入视野」是整族词背后的动词，由 ad-「向」与 parere「出现」构成。

items.en: French forms the noun aparance from the verb, and English takes the pattern with its own suffix -ance.
items.cn: 法语由这个动词造出名词 aparance，英语则用带着自己后缀 -ance 的形式接过来。

items.en: English appearance is first recorded in the sense 'the act of appearing', close to the verb.
items.cn: 英语 appearance 最初有记载的义项是「出现这一行为」，与动词义贴近。

items.en: The sense 'outward look' becomes common, and the word starts to judge as well as to describe.
items.cn: 「外表、外观」义变得常见，这个词开始既描述也评判。

items.en: The noun covers stage, court, publication and surface impression; the phrase to all appearances marks the doubt.
items.cn: 这个名词覆盖舞台、法庭、出版与表面印象；短语 to all appearances 则标出那份怀疑。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the family from the same Latin verb; the near-meaning group gathers words for presence, look and show.
note.cn: 形近组收同出那个拉丁动词的一族词；近义组收表示到场、外观与表象的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to come into sight or to seem.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「出现；显得」，本词由它加 -ance 构成。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning visible or merely seeming.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明显的」或「表面上的」，与本词同根。

entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「看来；据说」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: The state of being in a place and noticed there.
entries.definitionCN: 在场并被注意到的状态，对应 appearance 的「到场」义。

entries.definition: The act of reaching a place, often the moment of being seen.
entries.definitionCN: 到达某处的行为，常指被看见的那一刻。

entries.definition: An outward front, often hiding what is behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 对外的门面，常遮住背后的实情，与 appearance 的「表面现象」义接近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real appear-plus-ance structure and the frames the noun occupies.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的 appear 加 -ance 结构，以及这个名词占据的句式。

normal.en: It is appear plus -ance: the event of coming into view.
normal.cn: 它是 appear 加 -ance：进入视野这一事件。

normal.en: The event turns into a surface: what appears is also how a thing looks.
normal.cn: 事件转成表面：显现出来的样子，也就是一物的外观。

normal.en: Public life counts appearances: make an appearance, a public appearance.
normal.cn: 公共生活要算计露面：make an appearance、a public appearance。

normal.en: Books and players both appear; the noun marks the arrival.
normal.cn: 书与演员都会「出现」，这个名词标记的就是那次到来。

normal.en: The hedge phrase is to all appearances, meaning as far as one can see.
normal.cn: 留余地的短语是 to all appearances，意为「从表面看」。

abstract.en: Picture a figure stepping from shadow into a pool of light, and that pool becoming his identity.
abstract.cn: 想象一个身影从暗处走进光里，而那团光随后成了他的身份。

abstract.en: The word is a surface offered to other eyes, never the whole person.
abstract.cn: 这个词是递给他人目光的一个表面，从来不是整个的人。

abstract.en: Hence its caution: appearance can be a door or a mask, and the noun does not say which.
abstract.cn: 由此生出谨慎：外表可能是一扇门，也可能是一张面具，而这个名词并不说明是哪一种。

examples.en: Her appearance on stage was greeted with a long round of applause.
examples.cn: 她在台上的登场赢得了一长阵掌声。

examples.en: The building has changed little in appearance.
examples.cn: 这栋楼在外观上几乎没有变化。

examples.en: He made a brief appearance at the reception.
examples.cn: 他在招待会上短暂露了一面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额皮尔然斯」——演员皮尔从幕后走到灯下，全场看见他的样子：出现；外表

root: appearance 由 appear 加名词后缀 -ance 构成，而 appear 经古法语 aparoir 来自拉丁语 apparere「进入视野、显现」，该动词由 ad-「向」与 parere「出现」构成。十四世纪英语最初义为「出现这一行为」；十六世纪「外表、外观」义变得常见，这个词开始既描述也评判；现代它覆盖舞台、法庭、出版与表面印象，短语 to all appearances 标出其中的怀疑。

sensesIntro.en: Five uses fan out from one event of appearing: the act itself, the surface it leaves behind, a public visit, a performance or publication, and the impression that may differ from fact.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个用法从「出现」这一事件展开：行为本身、它留下的表面、公开到场、演出或问世，以及可能与事实不符的印象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure stepping from shadow into light, and that light becoming the face others know.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个身影从暗处走进光里，而那团光成了别人认识的那张脸。

branches.en: THE EVENT LINE: the bare act of becoming visible.
branches.cn: 事件线：变得可见这一赤裸的行为。

branches.en: THE SURFACE LINE: the event hardens into a lasting look.
branches.cn: 表面线：事件凝固成一个持久的外观。

branches.en: THE VISIT LINE: being seen once in public carries weight.
branches.cn: 到访线：在公众面前被看见一次就有分量。

branches.en: THE STAGE LINE: a player or a book arrives before the public.
branches.cn: 舞台线：演员或一本书来到公众面前。

branches.en: THE MASK LINE: the surface may hide more than it shows.
branches.cn: 面具线：表面藏起的可能比展示的更多。

intro.en: Appearance is a transparent noun: the verb appear plus the Romance noun suffix -ance.
