definition_zh: 天哪；哎呀；唉呀（表示惊讶或强调的感叹词）
definition_en: an exclamation used to show surprise, wonder, or emphasis, as a mild substitute for God
core_image: 突然看见意外之事时脱口而出的轻轻一声惊叹
scene: 小男孩推开家门，发现桌上放着一个巨大的生日蛋糕，蜡烛已经点燃。 Gosh, I really wasn't expecting a party today!
sceneCN: 这里 gosh 是「天哪、哎呀」（第 1 个义项：表示惊讶的感叹词）；句意是男孩惊喜地喊出「天哪，我真没想到今天会有派对」。图中可辨识物件：生日蛋糕、蜡烛、餐桌。

pos.zh: 感叹词：天哪；哎呀；表示惊讶、赞叹或加强语气

collocations.zh: 我的天哪（较缓和的惊叹）

derivatives.zh: 同类委婉惊叹词，义为「天哪；哎呀」，与 gosh 功能相同，出自另一委婉替换
由 golly 加后缀构成的旧式玩偶名称，义为「布娃娃」，与惊叹义仅形式相关

senses.title: An exclamation of surprise
senses.definition: a mild exclamation showing surprise or astonishment at something unexpected
senses.definitionCN: 表示惊讶、震惊的委婉感叹词，用于遇到意料之外的事情时
senses.example: Gosh, I had no idea this old shop was still open.
senses.exampleCN: 天哪，我完全不知道这家老店还开着。
senses.why: People needed a way to cry out in surprise without using a sacred name, so a softened sound took over that job.
senses.whyCN: 人们需要一种不用神圣名字也能喊出惊讶的方式，于是用一个弱化了的音承担了这个功能。

senses.title: An exclamation of admiration
senses.definition: an exclamation expressing wonder, delight, or admiration for something impressive
senses.definitionCN: 表示赞叹、欣喜的感叹词，用于看到令人佩服或喜爱的事物时
senses.example: Gosh, what a beautiful view from the top of the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 哇，山顶上的景色真美。
senses.why: The same burst of breath that signals shock also signals delight; only the feeling behind it changes.
senses.whyCN: 同一声脱口而出的气息既能表达震惊也能表达欣喜，区别只在背后的情绪。

senses.title: A mild intensifier
senses.definition: an exclamation used mainly to add emphasis or make a statement sound more sincere
senses.definitionCN: 主要用于加强语气或让话语听起来更真诚的感叹词
senses.example: Gosh, it was kind of you to drive all this way to help.
senses.exampleCN: 说真的，你专程开车过来帮忙，真是太好了。
senses.why: Once the exclamation becomes habitual, it drifts into pure emphasis, coloring the sentence rather than reacting to it.
senses.whyCN: 当这声感叹变成习惯用语后，它就滑向纯粹的加强语气，不再对具体事物作出反应，而是给整句话上色。

senses.title: A polite substitute for God
senses.titleCN: 委婉替换：避免直呼神圣之名
senses.definition: a euphemistic replacement for the word God, used to avoid taking a sacred name in vain
senses.definitionCN: 作为 God 的委婉替换词，用于避免直呼神圣之名，语气更礼貌得体
senses.example: She caught herself and said gosh instead of the sacred name.
senses.exampleCN: 她及时收住，改口说了声 gosh，没有直呼那个神圣的名字。
senses.why: The word was created precisely for this purpose: to keep the exclamation but strip away the sacred name inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词正是为此目的而造：保留惊叹的功能，但去掉其中神圣的名字。

senses.title: An expression of dismay
senses.definition: an exclamation used when something goes wrong, showing mild frustration or dismay
senses.definitionCN: 用于事情出岔子时表示轻微沮丧或懊恼的感叹词
senses.example: Gosh, I've left my keys on the bus again.
senses.exampleCN: 唉呀，我又把钥匙落在公交车上了。
senses.why: Surprise and frustration share the same trigger: reality breaks your expectation, and the word escapes before you can think.
senses.whyCN: 惊讶与懊恼的触发点相同：现实打破了预期，这个词在你来得及思考之前就脱口而出。

senses.title: A softener in conversation
senses.definition: an exclamation used to soften a question or statement and make it sound friendlier
senses.definitionCN: 用于软化提问或陈述语气、使话语显得更亲切随和的感叹词
senses.example: Gosh, could you tell me how to get to the station?
senses.exampleCN: 请问，您能告诉我车站怎么走吗？
senses.why: The sound is short and gentle, so speakers place it at the front of a sentence to lower its edge.
senses.whyCN: 这个音短促而柔和，说话人把它放在句首，用来磨平句子生硬的棱角。

senses.title: Storybook and children's speech
senses.definition: an exclamation strongly associated with children's speech, old comics, and polite storybook dialogue
senses.definitionCN: 带有儿童口语、旧式漫画和礼貌童话对白色彩的感叹词
senses.example: In the old comics, the hero always cried gosh when the villain appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧漫画里，每当反派出现，主角总会喊一声 gosh。
senses.why: Because it is inoffensive, writers gave it to children and polite characters, and that image stuck.
senses.whyCN: 因为它毫无冒犯性，作者们把它分配给孩子和彬彬有礼的角色，这种形象便固定了下来。

senses.title: By gosh: stubborn emphasis
senses.definition: in the phrase by gosh, used to insist on one's point with folksy determination
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 by gosh，以朴素的固执语气坚持自己的说法
senses.example: He promised that by gosh he would finish rebuilding the fence before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他保证说，无论如何也要赶在冬天前把栅栏修好。
senses.why: Swearing formulas like by God became softened into by gosh, keeping the insisting frame without the sacred word.
senses.whyCN: by God 一类起誓句式被弱化为 by gosh，保留了坚持表态的框架，却去掉了神圣的词。

intro.en: Gosh is a deliberately softened exclamation: English speakers altered the name of God so that they could cry out without taking it in vain.
intro.cn: gosh 是刻意弱化出来的感叹词：英语使用者改动了 God 的读音，以便既能脱口惊呼又不至于妄称神名。

items.en: *ghut- or *ghau- is generally reconstructed as the root behind the verb 'to call' and the noun 'that which is invoked'; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *ghut- 或 *ghau- 是「呼喊」动词及「被呼唤者」名词背后的词根；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The word god, meaning the deity, was already in use; it may have developed from the calling root, though earlier explanations linked it to a Gothic tribal name.
items.cn: 表示神祇的 god 一词已在古英语中使用；一般认为它源自「呼喊」词根，但也有早期解释把它与哥特部落名联系起来。

items.en: Swearing by God was widespread and was widely condemned as blasphemy, so speakers began distorting the sacred name into softened forms.
items.cn: 以 God 起誓十分普遍，又普遍被斥为亵渎，于是说话人开始把神圣之名扭曲成弱化形式。

items.en: The spelling gosh is first recorded in 1757; the exact date of its spoken origin is uncertain, and it likely circulated in speech earlier.
items.cn: 拼写形式 gosh 首见于 1757 年的记录；其口头起源的确切年代不确定，可能在此之前已在口语中流传。

items.en: Alongside gosh grew a whole family of softened exclamations such as golly and gollywog, all built by altering a name or sound rather than inventing a root.
items.cn: 十九世纪前后，gosh 周围长出一整族弱化惊叹词，如 golly 和 gollywog，它们都靠改动名字或读音构成，而非新造词根。

items.en: Today gosh survives mostly in children's speech, storybooks, and gently old-fashioned dialogue, while stronger exclamations have taken over elsewhere.
items.cn: 如今 gosh 主要保留在儿童口语、童话故事和略带旧式的礼貌对白中，其他场合已被更强的惊叹词取代。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers softened exclamations and sound-alike words; the near-meaning group gathers other mild cries of surprise.
note.cn: 形近组收同一类弱化惊叹词与发音相近的词；近义组收其他表示轻微惊讶的感叹词。

entries.definition: A British mild exclamation of surprise, formed by the same softening process as gosh.
entries.definitionCN: 英式温和惊叹词，义为「天哪」，与 gosh 出自同一种弱化改音手法。

entries.definition: An old-fashioned name for a type of doll; it borrows golly but has nothing to do with surprise.
entries.definitionCN: 旧式玩偶的名称，义为「布娃娃」；借用了 golly 一词，但与惊讶之义无关。

entries.definition: A long deep cut or wound; merely sounds close and comes from another root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「深长的伤口；划开」；只是发音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A fierce hunting hawk; the first element is Old English for goose, unrelated to the exclamation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「苍鹰」；首成分是古英语「鹅」一词，与感叹词 gosh 无关。

entries.definition: Thin transparent fabric; its spelling and sound resemble gosh but its origin lies elsewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「纱布、薄纱」；拼写与发音和 gosh 相近，但词源毫不相干。

entries.definition: A mild American exclamation of surprise, likewise softened from Jesus.
entries.definitionCN: 美式温和惊叹词，义为「哎呀」，同样由 Jesus 弱化而来。

entries.definition: A strong exclamation of astonishment or admiration, without any religious background.
entries.definitionCN: 表示惊叹或赞叹的强烈感叹词，义为「哇」，没有任何宗教背景。

entries.definition: A polite exclamation of surprise, itself a shortened softened form of oh my God.
entries.definitionCN: 表示惊讶的礼貌感叹语，义为「我的天」，本身是 oh my God 的缩短弱化形式。

entries.definition: A dated exclamation of surprise that points upward instead of naming God directly.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧式的惊讶感叹词，义为「天哪」，以「上天」指代而不直呼神名。

entries.definition: A mild exclamation built on the abstract quality of God, as in goodness me.
entries.definitionCN: 温和感叹词，以「上帝的善性」婉转代称，如 goodness me 表示「天哪」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real softening of the name of God and the phrases where the word actually appears.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「God 的弱化」这一真实来历，以及这个词实际出现的常见短语。

normal.en: gosh is God with the ending changed: the exclamation keeps the cry but drops the sacred name.
normal.cn: gosh 就是 God 改了词尾：惊叹保留下来，神圣之名被换掉了。

normal.en: oh my gosh is the polite twin of oh my God.
normal.cn: oh my gosh 是 oh my God 的礼貌版本。

normal.en: The same softening family gives gee (from Jesus) and golly, all mild cries of surprise.
normal.cn: 同一弱化家族还产出 gee（源自 Jesus）和 golly，都是温和的惊呼声。

normal.en: by gosh keeps the old swearing frame 'by God' in a folksy softened way.
normal.cn: by gosh 以朴素弱化的方式保留了 by God 这一古老的起誓句式。

normal.en: Old comics give gosh to children and polite heroes, so the word carries an innocent flavor.
normal.cn: 旧漫画把 gosh 留给孩子和礼貌的主角，因此这个词自带天真无害的色彩。

abstract.en: Picture a small child lifting both hands at a birthday cake, letting out one soft syllable of pure surprise.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小孩面对生日蛋糕举起双手，轻轻吐出一声纯粹的惊讶。

abstract.en: Hear the difference: one word shouts a sacred name, the other lets the air out gently, like a valve releasing pressure slowly.
abstract.cn: 听听两者的差别：一个词喊出神圣之名，另一个把气轻轻放掉，像阀门缓缓释放压力。

abstract.en: Gosh is a cushion between you and the shock: the event hits, and the soft sound absorbs it.
abstract.cn: gosh 是你与震惊之间的一块软垫：事件砸过来，柔和的一声把它吸收掉。

examples.en: Gosh, I had no idea this old shop was still open.
examples.cn: 天哪，我完全不知道这家老店还开着。

examples.en: Gosh, it was kind of you to drive all this way to help.
examples.cn: 说真的，你专程开车过来帮忙，真是太好了。

examples.en: The villagers still tell how the frightened child simply said gosh and then burst out laughing.
examples.cn: 村民至今还在讲，当年那个受惊的孩子只轻轻说了声「天哪」，接着便大笑起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「高什」——高，什（什么）！看到高处 unexpected 的东西脱口喊一声：天哪

root: gosh 是 God 的委婉弱化形式：把神圣之名的词尾改掉，保留惊叹功能而避免妄称神名。God 源自古英语 god「神」，一般追溯至原始印欧语表示「呼喊」的词根 *ghut- 或 *ghau-（重构形式，更早来源不确定）。与 golly、gee 等同属十九世纪前后的弱化惊叹词家族。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of gosh all grow from one softened cry: it signals surprise, delight, dismay, polite emphasis, and the innocent flavor of storybook speech.
sensesIntro.cn: gosh 的各个义项都从一声弱化的惊呼长出：它表示惊讶、赞叹、懊恼、礼貌的强调，以及童话语言的天真色彩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft burst of breath escaping at an unexpected sight, like a valve gently releasing pressure.
core.cn: 核心意象：看到意外之事时轻轻呼出的一口气，像阀门缓缓释放压力。

branches.en: THE REACTION: unexpected events pull out the cry, whether the feeling is astonishment or mild dismay.
branches.cn: 反应线：意外之事逼出这声惊呼，情绪可以是震惊也可以是轻微懊恼。

branches.en: THE DELIGHT: the same breath turns admiring when the sight pleases instead of shocks.
branches.cn: 赞叹线：当所见令人欣喜而非震惊，同一声气息便转为赞叹。

branches.en: THE EMPHASIS: habitual use makes the word a soft intensifier and keeps the old swearing frame in by gosh.
branches.cn: 强调线：习惯化使这个词成为柔和的语气词，并在 by gosh 中保留古老的起誓框架。

branches.en: THE SUBSTITUTE: the word exists precisely to replace the sacred name while keeping the cry.
branches.cn: 替换线：这个词的存在意义正是替下神圣之名，同时保留惊叹。

branches.en: THE TONE: its softness softens questions and marks children's speech and storybook dialogue.
branches.cn: 语气线：它的柔和既可软化提问，也标示出儿童口语与童话对白的色彩。

intro.en: Gosh has no prefix or suffix: it is an altered form of the name of God, and its family is built by sound change rather than affixation.
intro.cn: gosh 没有前缀或后缀：它是 God 之名的改音形式，其词族靠读音变化而非词缀构词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word belongs to this family; the lineage runs through Old English god and a reconstructed Indo-European root, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词族没有拉丁同源词；其谱系经由古英语 god 与重构的印欧词根，因此拉丁同源词列表为空。

items.meaning: the deity; the name being softened
items.example: Gosh alters this name to soften the exclamation.
items.exampleCN: gosh 通过改动这个名字来弱化惊叹。

items.example: The root is generally reconstructed behind god.
items.exampleCN: 一般认为这个重构词根是 god 的来源。

items.meaning: changed ending used to soften a name
items.meaningCN: 弱化词尾：靠改音代替神名
items.example: God becomes gosh by altering the ending.
items.exampleCN: God 改变词尾就成了 gosh。

items.example: Golly grew beside gosh in the same softening family.
items.exampleCN: golly 与 gosh 出自同一弱化家族。

items.meaning: a mild cry softened from Jesus
items.meaningCN: 由 Jesus 弱化来的温和惊呼声
items.example: Gee shows the same process applied to another sacred name.
items.exampleCN: gee 显示同样的手法用在另一个神圣之名上。

items.meaning: polite version of oh my God
items.meaningCN: oh my God 的礼貌版本
items.example: Oh my gosh, the cake is enormous!
items.exampleCN: 我的天哪，这蛋糕太大了！

items.meaning: folksy insistence, softened from by God
items.meaningCN: 由 by God 弱化来的朴素强调句式
items.example: By gosh, the fence will be finished.
items.exampleCN: 无论如何，栅栏一定会修完。

items.meaningCN: 极糟的（旧式俚语复合形容词）
items.example: The old play was gosh-awful, the critics said.
items.exampleCN: 评论家说那出旧戏糟糕透顶。

definition_zh: 大惊小怪；忙乱；抱怨
definition_en: unnecessary excitement, worry, or activity about something small
core_image: 一家人为一道小划痕忙作一团
scene: 一道小划痕不值得这么大惊小怪。 A small scratch is not worth all this fuss.
sceneCN: 这里 fuss 是「大惊小怪」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一道小划痕不值得这么大惊小怪。

senses.title: Needless excitement
senses.definition: too much excitement or worry about something unimportant
senses.definitionCN: 对不重要的事情表现出过多的激动或担心
senses.example: A small scratch is not worth all this fuss.
senses.exampleCN: 一道小划痕不值得这么大惊小怪。
senses.why: This is the central sense of needless worry.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示不必要担心的核心义项。

senses.title: Busy movement
senses.definition: a lot of hurried activity, often about small matters
senses.definitionCN: 大量匆忙的活动，常为琐事
senses.example: There was a fuss in the kitchen before dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭前厨房里一片忙乱。
senses.why: The word also names the bustle itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也指忙乱本身。

senses.title: Complain or worry
senses.definition: to complain or worry about something in an annoying way
senses.definitionCN: 以令人厌烦的方式抱怨或担心某事
senses.example: She fussed about the seat all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 她整个晚上都在为座位抱怨。
senses.why: As a verb it describes the complaining.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时描述这种抱怨。

intro.en: Fuss appeared in English in the early modern period, and its origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: fuss 在近代英语早期出现，来源并不确定。

items.en: The word first appeared in the early eighteenth century.
items.cn: 这个词最早出现于十八世纪初。

items.en: It first meant a busy bustle.
items.cn: 它最初指忙乱的活动。

items.en: It came to mean needless excitement.
items.cn: 它逐渐表示不必要的激动。

items.en: Make a fuss became a common phrase.
items.cn: make a fuss 成为常用短语。

items.en: Fuss over someone shows anxious care.
items.cn: fuss over 某人表示过分担忧的关心。

note.en: Fuss is compared with look-alike words and words for needless trouble.
note.cn: 把 fuss 与形近词以及表示无谓麻烦的词作比较。

entries.definition: a safety part in an electrical circuit
entries.definitionCN: 保险丝

entries.definition: hard to please
entries.definitionCN: 挑剔的

entries.definition: a closed hand
entries.definitionCN: 拳头

entries.definition: noisy activity and confusion
entries.definitionCN: 骚动

entries.definition: trouble or effort
entries.definitionCN: 麻烦

entries.definition: a statement that something is wrong
entries.definitionCN: 抱怨

normalIntro.en: Fuss is noise and worry out of proportion to the problem.
normalIntro.cn: fuss 是与问题不成比例的喧闹和担心。

normal.en: A small scratch is not worth all this fuss.
normal.cn: 一道小划痕不值得这么大惊小怪。

normal.en: There was a fuss in the kitchen before dinner.
normal.cn: 晚饭前厨房里一片忙乱。

normal.en: She fussed about the seat all evening.
normal.cn: 她整个晚上都在为座位抱怨。

normal.en: He made a fuss over a tiny mistake.
normal.cn: 他为一个极小的错误大惊小怪。

normal.en: The nurse fussed over the patient kindly.
normal.cn: 护士亲切地围着病人忙碌。

abstract.en: A fuss is a storm in a teacup.
abstract.cn: 大惊小怪就像茶杯里的风暴。

abstract.en: Noise often measures fear, not importance.
abstract.cn: 喧闹常常衡量的是恐惧，而不是重要性。

abstract.en: The calm person saves the fuss for what matters.
abstract.cn: 沉稳的人把大惊小怪留给真正重要的事。

examples.en: A small scratch is not worth all this fuss.
examples.cn: 一道小划痕不值得这么大惊小怪。

examples.en: There was a fuss in the kitchen before dinner.
examples.cn: 晚饭前厨房里一片忙乱。

examples.en: She fussed about the seat all evening.
examples.cn: 她整个晚上都在为座位抱怨。

dict_mnemonic.text: fuss 与 fuse、fussy 形近；make a fuss 是「大惊小怪」，fuss over 是「过分关心」。

root: 近代英语早期出现的词，来源不确定；核心义「为小事而生的忙乱与抱怨」。

sensesIntro.en: Fuss is needless excitement, busy movement, or the act of complaining.
sensesIntro.cn: fuss 指不必要的激动、忙乱的活动，或抱怨的行为。

core.en: Energy spent on something too small for it.
core.cn: 花在过小之事上的精力。

branches.en: A scratch draws far too much worry.
branches.cn: 一道划痕引来过多担心。

branches.en: The kitchen fills with hurried steps.
branches.cn: 厨房里满是匆忙的脚步。

branches.en: Someone complains without end.
branches.cn: 有人没完没了地抱怨。

branches.en: Worry shows itself as busy movement.
branches.cn: 担心表现为忙乱的动作。

branches.en: Needless excitement becomes a complaint.
branches.cn: 不必要的激动变成抱怨。

intro.en: Fuss builds words for being picky and for busy care.
intro.cn: fuss 构成表示挑剔和忙碌关照的词。

latinIntro.en: Fuss is not a Latin word and has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: fuss 不是拉丁词，没有拉丁词根。

items.example: The fuss lasted only a minute.
items.exampleCN: 这阵忙乱只持续了一分钟。

items.example: He fusses whenever guests arrive.
items.exampleCN: 每次有客人来他都要忙乱一番。

items.example: She fussed all morning about the trip.
items.exampleCN: 她整个上午都在为旅行操心。

items.example: Stop fussing and sit down.
items.exampleCN: 别瞎忙了，坐下吧。

items.example: The baby is fussy tonight.
items.exampleCN: 宝宝今晚很闹人。

items.example: He arranged the cups fussily.
items.exampleCN: 他大惊小怪地摆好杯子。

items.example: Her fussiness about food is well known.
items.exampleCN: 她对食物的挑剔是出了名的。

items.example: The trip was simple and fuss-free.
items.exampleCN: 这趟旅行简单又省心。

definition_zh: 厌恶；使厌恶
definition_en: a strong feeling of dislike, or to make someone feel this
core_image: 一个人闻到坏掉的食物，脸往后一缩
scene: 他低头闻了闻那碗放了三天的汤，立刻把脸转开。 The smell of the bin filled her with disgust.
sceneCN: 这里 disgust 指「厌恶」（第 1 个义项：强烈的反感）；句意是垃圾桶的气味让她满心厌恶。

senses.title: A strong feeling of dislike
senses.definition: a strong feeling of dislike caused by something unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 由不快之物引起的强烈反感
senses.example: She turned away in disgust.
senses.exampleCN: 她厌恶地转过身。
senses.why: The body pulls back before the mind finds a word.
senses.whyCN: 身体先退开，脑子才找到词。

senses.title: To cause that feeling
senses.definition: to make someone feel strong dislike
senses.definitionCN: 让人产生强烈反感
senses.example: The mess disgusted everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 那堆脏乱让屋里每个人都反感。
senses.why: A smell can push a whole room toward the door.
senses.whyCN: 一种气味能把整屋子人推向门口。

intro.en: Disgust comes from Old French desgouster, to lose the taste for something, from des- and goust, taste.
intro.cn: disgust 来自古法语 desgouster（失去胃口），由 des- 与 goust（味道）构成。

items.en: Gustus meant taste, and gustare meant to taste.
items.cn: gustus 指味道，gustare 指品尝。

items.en: Desgouster meant to lose the taste for something.
items.cn: 古法语 desgouster 指对某物失去胃口。

items.en: English disgust meant a strong distaste.
items.cn: 英语 disgust 指强烈的反胃感。

items.en: The verb added the sense of causing that distaste.
items.cn: 动词又添上使人产生这种反感的意思。

items.en: It now covers moral repulsion as well as bad food.
items.cn: 今天它既指食物难吃，也指道德上的反感。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on Latin gustus, taste, and the meaning group names stronger forms of dislike.
note.cn: 形近组建在拉丁语 gustus（味道）上，近义组列出更强的反感。

entries.definition: a sudden rush of wind
entries.definitionCN: 突然刮起的一阵风

entries.definition: lively enjoyment in doing something
entries.definitionCN: 做事时的痛快劲

entries.definition: causing strong dislike
entries.definitionCN: 引起强烈反感的

entries.definition: a very strong feeling of disgust
entries.definitionCN: 极强烈的厌恶

entries.definition: a mild dislike of something
entries.definitionCN: 轻微的反感

entries.definition: to drive someone away by being unpleasant
entries.definitionCN: 因令人不快而使人退开

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a bowl gone bad and end with a whole room stepping back.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一碗变质的汤开始，落到整屋子人一起后退。

normal.en: Dis- plus gust: the taste turns against you.
normal.cn: dis 加 gust，味道反过来对付你。

normal.en: Milk left out for a day can disgust a child.
normal.cn: 牛奶在外放一天，能让孩子反胃。

normal.en: A dirty kitchen disgusts more than a loud argument.
normal.cn: 脏厨房比大声争吵更让人反感。

normal.en: Disgusted, he pushed the plate away unseen.
normal.cn: 他一阵反感，悄悄把盘子推开。

normal.en: Some lies disgust people who tell small ones daily.
normal.cn: 有些谎话会让天天说小谎的人也反感。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon lifted and then set down fast.
abstract.cn: 想象勺子举起又飞快放下。

abstract.en: Picture a face turned toward the window.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸转向窗户。

abstract.en: Picture a hand held over the nose and mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手捂住口鼻。

examples.en: The smell of the bin filled her with disgust.
examples.cn: 垃圾桶的气味让她满心厌恶。

examples.en: He looked at the dirty plate in disgust.
examples.cn: 他厌恶地看着那只脏盘子。

examples.en: The state of the kitchen disgusted the inspector.
examples.cn: 厨房的状况让检查员十分反感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disgust 记成「坏了胃口」：dis 表示相反，gust 是味道，尝到坏味道就反胃，进而厌恶。

root: 来自古法语 desgouster（失去胃口），由 des-（相反）与 goust（味道）构成，goust 可追到拉丁语 gustus。本义是食物让人反胃，后来从口舌的感觉扩展到对行为与人品的强烈反感。

sensesIntro.en: From a mouth that refuses food to a mind that refuses a deed.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一张拒绝食物的嘴，到一颗拒绝某种行为的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face pulled back from a bowl that has gone bad.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张脸从变质的碗边往后缩。

branches.en: The first sense is the feeling inside the body.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是身体里升起的那种感觉。

branches.en: The second sense is the thing that puts it there.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把它放进身体的那件事。

branches.en: Both senses turn on a loss of appetite.
branches.cn: 两个义项都围绕胃口的失去。

branches.en: Both begin in the nose before they reach the mind.
branches.cn: 两个义项都先到鼻子，再到心里。

branches.en: Only the second sense needs an object in front of you.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项需要眼前有个对象。

intro.en: Disgust belongs to the Latin gustus family, where taste and wind share one small stem.
intro.cn: disgust 属于拉丁语 gustus 一族，味道与一阵风共用同一个小词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin gustus, taste, gives goust in French and gust in English, and des- turns taste into its opposite.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gustus（味道）在法语里成为 goust，在英语里成为 gust，前缀 des- 把味道翻成反面。

items.meaning: to lose the taste for something
items.example: The smell disgusted him.
items.exampleCN: 那气味让他反感。

items.example: A gust shook the window.
items.exampleCN: 一阵风摇着窗户。

items.example: She sang with gusto.
items.exampleCN: 她唱得很有劲头。

items.example: He was disgusted by the lie.
items.exampleCN: 那个谎话让他反感。

items.example: A disgusting smell rose from the drain.
items.exampleCN: 下水道冒出一股难闻的气味。

items.example: The room was disgustingly dirty.
items.exampleCN: 房间脏得令人反感。

items.meaning: relating to the sense of taste
items.example: Gustatory nerves carry flavour.
items.exampleCN: 味觉神经传递味道。

items.example: He spoke with distaste.
items.exampleCN: 他带着反感说话。

definition_zh: 易受伤害的；脆弱的；易受攻击的；易患病的
definition_en: easily hurt, attacked, or harmed, either physically or emotionally
core_image: 露出的伤口：护甲裂开一道缝，谁碰谁疼
scene: 暴雨中，帐篷的绳结松脱了。 The old bridge is vulnerable to flooding after heavy rain.
sceneCN: 这里 vulnerable 是「易受伤害的」（第 1 个义项：容易受到损害）；句意是暴雨之后，这座旧桥容易被洪水破坏。

pos.zh: 形容词：易受伤害的；脆弱的；易受攻击的；易患病的

collocations.zh: 使某人处于易受伤害的境地

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「脆弱性、易受伤害性」，由形容词加抽象名词后缀构成
形容词，义为「无法伤害的、刀枪不入的」，由否定前缀 in- 加本词构成
副词，义为「脆弱地」，由形容词加副词后缀构成

senses.title: Easily harmed physically
senses.titleCN: 易受伤害的：容易受到物理损害
senses.definition: easily damaged or hurt by physical forces or events
senses.definitionCN: 容易被物理力量或事件损害
senses.example: The old bridge is vulnerable to flooding after heavy rain.
senses.exampleCN: 暴雨之后，这座旧桥容易被洪水破坏。
senses.why: Latin vulnus means a wound; a woundable thing is one harm can reach.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vulnus 意为伤口；可受伤之物就是伤害能够抵达的东西。

senses.title: Weak against attack
senses.titleCN: 易受攻击的：防御上存在弱点
senses.definition: open to being attacked or criticized, with weak defenses
senses.definitionCN: 防御薄弱，容易受到攻击或批评
senses.example: The network was vulnerable because one server had no password.
senses.exampleCN: 这个网络很脆弱，因为一台服务器没设密码。
senses.why: Where armor has a gap, the blow lands; the wound-word names the reachable spot.
senses.whyCN: 护甲有缝之处打击便能命中，「伤口」一词正指向那个可及之处。

senses.title: Emotionally exposed
senses.titleCN: 情感上脆弱的：内心容易受伤
senses.definition: easily hurt in feelings, or willing to show feelings openly
senses.definitionCN: 情感上容易受伤，或愿意坦诚展露内心
senses.example: She felt vulnerable talking about her childhood in public.
senses.exampleCN: 她当众谈起童年时，感到内心脆弱而暴露。
senses.why: The heart can be wounded as the body can; the metaphor moves from skin to soul.
senses.whyCN: 心也会像身体一样受伤，比喻由皮肤延伸到灵魂。

senses.title: At risk in a population
senses.titleCN: 易患病的：身体上易受疾病侵袭
senses.definition: at risk of catching a disease or being harmed by conditions
senses.definitionCN: 容易患病或被不良条件伤害的（人群、个体）
senses.example: Babies and the elderly are especially vulnerable to the virus.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿和老人特别容易感染这种病毒。
senses.why: A body already weak takes wounds sooner; susceptibility is woundedness waiting.
senses.whyCN: 已经虚弱的身体更容易受伤，易感性就是「等着发生的伤口」。

senses.title: In a weak social position
senses.titleCN: 弱势的：社会处境容易受损害
senses.definition: in a position of disadvantage where harm or loss is more likely
senses.definitionCN: 处于不利地位、更容易受到损失或伤害的
senses.example: Voluntary groups protect vulnerable members of society.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿组织保护社会中的弱势成员。
senses.why: Without resources, armor, or allies, every blow reaches the person beneath.
senses.whyCN: 缺少资源、防护与盟友，每一记打击都能直接落到那个人身上。

intro.en: Vulnerable comes from Latin vulnus, a wound, probably related to vellere, to pluck or tear, though the exact link is generally believed rather than proven.
intro.cn: vulnerable 源自拉丁语 vulnus（伤口），一般认为与 vellere（拔、撕扯）相关，但确切联系属于普遍推定而非定论。

items.en: The reconstructed root behind vellere means to tear or pluck; its connection to the wound-word is a commonly accepted hypothesis.
items.cn: vellere 背后的重构词根意为撕扯、拔取；它与「伤口」一词的联系是普遍接受的假说。

items.en: Vulnus means a wound; the adjective vulnerabilis means able to be wounded.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vulnus 意为伤口；形容词 vulnerabilis 意为可被弄伤的。

items.en: Vulnerabilis passes into late Latin usage as a descriptive term for anything woundable.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中，vulnerabilis 用作描述任何可受伤之物的词语。

items.en: English borrows vulnerable in military writing first, for cities and troops open to attack.
items.cn: 英语最初在军事文本中借入 vulnerable，指易受攻击的城市与军队。

items.en: The sense spreads to emotional hurt and to people exposed to disease or hardship.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪，词义扩展到情感伤害及易患病、易受困的人群。

items.en: Vulnerable now names weak points everywhere, from vulnerable groups to vulnerable software.
items.cn: 如今 vulnerable 指一切薄弱之处，从弱势群体到有漏洞的软件。

note.en: Vulnerable stands beside its Latin wound-family and the risk word-field; look-alikes share the root, near meanings share the field of exposure to harm.
note.cn: vulnerable 与拉丁「伤口」词族及「风险」义场相邻：形近组共享词根，近义组共享「暴露于伤害」义场。

entries.definition: impossible to harm or attack successfully
entries.definitionCN: 刀枪不入的、无法伤害的；加否定前缀 in- 构成，义与本词相反

entries.definition: the quality of being easily hurt, or a specific weak point
entries.definitionCN: 脆弱性、漏洞；由 vulnerable 加抽象名词后缀构成

entries.definition: an injury caused by a weapon; to inflict such an injury
entries.definitionCN: 伤口、使受伤；日耳曼词源，与 vulnerable 义场相邻但词源不同，拼写易混

entries.definition: a large bird that feeds on carrion
entries.definitionCN: 秃鹫；与本词开头字母相同、易在拼写上混淆，但词源完全不同

entries.definition: lacking refinement, or relating to ordinary people
entries.definitionCN: 粗俗的、大众的；词首拼形相近，源自 vulgus（民众），词源不同

entries.definition: left without cover or protection
entries.definitionCN: 暴露的、无遮蔽的；强调缺少保护这一状态

entries.definition: easily broken or damaged
entries.definitionCN: 易碎的、脆弱的；侧重物体易碎，vulnerable 兼指人

entries.definition: easily affected by something, such as disease or influence
entries.definitionCN: 易受影响的、易感染的；侧重易感性

entries.definition: having no way to protect yourself
entries.definitionCN: 毫无防备的、手无寸铁的；强调没有防御手段

entries.definition: in danger of being harmed
entries.definitionCN: 处于危险中的；口语与官方文件常用的短语式近义

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Latin wound-family of vulnus.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，全部来自拉丁语 vulnus（伤口）词族。

normal.en: vulnus means wound; vulnerable literally means wound-able.
normal.cn: vulnus 意为伤口；vulnerable 字面就是「可受伤的」。

normal.en: invulnerable flips it with in-: wound-proof, like armor.
normal.cn: invulnerable 用 in- 反转它：防伤的，如同铠甲。

normal.en: vulnerability is the noun: the state of being woundable.
normal.cn: vulnerability 是它的名词形式：可受伤这种状态。

normal.en: the stress of the word sits on the first syllable: VUL-nerable.
normal.cn: 这个词的重音在第一个音节：VUL-nerable。

normal.en: the phrase vulnerable to something is the common frame: open to that harm.
normal.cn: 常见搭配 vulnerable to something：对那种伤害敞开着。

abstract.en: Picture armor with one cracked seam: light, rain, and hands all find it.
abstract.cn: 想象护甲上裂开的一道缝：光线、雨水、他人之手都能找到它。

abstract.en: A peeled fruit in an open market: anything may touch it first.
abstract.cn: 市场上削了皮的水果：谁都可能先碰到它。

abstract.en: Saying a secret out loud makes the chest a wound the world can enter.
abstract.cn: 把秘密说出口的那一刻，胸膛便成了世界可以进入的伤口。

examples.en: Young birds are vulnerable to predators until they can fly.
examples.cn: 幼鸟在学会飞行之前容易受捕食者伤害。

examples.en: He became emotionally vulnerable after the divorce.
examples.cn: 离婚之后，他在情感上变得脆弱。

examples.en: The report listed vulnerable coastal towns facing rising seas.
examples.cn: 报告列出了面临海平面上升、易受损害的沿海城镇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我呢弱」——「我呢？弱呀。」护甲裂开一道缝时先承认自己弱，才能补上它。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自拉丁 vulnus（伤口）。

root: 拉丁语 vulnus（伤口）+ 形容词后缀 -abilis（可……的）构成 vulnerabilis（可被弄伤的），经晚期拉丁语进入英语。一般认为 vulnus 与动词 vellere（拔、撕扯）同源，但这一联系属于推定。同族词 invulnerable（加否定前缀 in-）、vulnerability 等。

sensesIntro.en: From the open wound outward: physical harm, weak defenses, exposed feelings, disease risk, and social disadvantage.
sensesIntro.cn: 从敞开的伤口向外铺开：物理损害、防御弱点、暴露的情感、患病风险，最后到社会处境的弱势。

definition_zh: 手机；移动电话；蜂窝电话
definition_en: a telephone that can be carried everywhere and works through a network of radio stations arranged in cells
core_image: 握在掌心的小窗：一块巴掌大的屏幕，把千里之外的人拉到耳边
scene: 地铁到站前，她把耳机塞进耳朵，低头看着屏幕上的未读消息轻轻微笑。 She checks every message on her cellphone before the train reaches the station.
sceneCN: 这里 cellphone 是「手机、移动电话」（第 1 个义项：随身携带的通话设备）；句意是她在地铁到站前查看手机上的每一条未读消息。

pos.zh: 手机；移动电话；蜂窝电话

derivatives.zh: 同义表达，mobile 源自拉丁 mobilis（可移动的），义为「移动电话」
由 cell 加形容词后缀构成，义为「蜂窝状的；细胞的」
由希腊词根 tele-（远）+ phone（声音）构成，义为「电话」

senses.title: A portable telephone
senses.definition: a small telephone that you can carry with you and use anywhere
senses.definitionCN: 可以随身携带、在任何地方使用的电话设备
senses.example: She left her cellphone at home and felt cut off all day.
senses.exampleCN: 她把手机忘在家里，一整天都觉得与世隔绝。
senses.why: The word joins cell, the radio zones of the network, with phone, sound; the object is literally a phone served by cells.
senses.whyCN: cellphone 由 cell（网络中的蜂窝小区）与 phone（声音）合成，字面义就是「由蜂窝小区提供服务的电话」，核心义项由此而来。

senses.title: The device as a personal tool
senses.definition: the device regarded as someone's personal property and daily companion
senses.definitionCN: 被视为个人财物与日常伴侣的那部手机
senses.example: My cellphone holds my photos, notes and timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 我的手机里存着我的照片、笔记和课程表。
senses.why: Once everyone owns one phone, the word shifts from a kind of device to that one device a person carries.
senses.whyCN: 当人手一部手机时，词义从「一类设备」滑向「某人随身的那一部」，泛指义收缩为特定义。

senses.title: Phone calls made on it
senses.definition: a call or conversation made using a cellphone
senses.definitionCN: 用手机打出的电话或进行的通话
senses.example: The interview was arranged over a cellphone.
senses.exampleCN: 这次面试是用手机电话约定的。
senses.why: In English a device often stands for the activity done with it, so cellphone can mean the call itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语里常用工具名词转指用它做的事，cellphone 借这种转喻从设备转指「通话」这一行为结果。

senses.title: Mobile communication in general
senses.definition: the technology or system of wireless mobile communication
senses.definitionCN: 无线移动通信的技术或体系
senses.example: The valley has no cellphone coverage.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷没有手机信号覆盖。
senses.why: Because the network, not just the handset, makes calls possible, the word also names the whole system.
senses.whyCN: 手机能通话依赖整张蜂窝网络，于是该词又扩展指「移动通信体系」，如信号、覆盖、制式。

senses.title: Used before another noun
senses.titleCN: 定语用法：手机的、手机用的
senses.definition: placed before a noun to show the noun belongs to the world of cellphones
senses.definitionCN: 置于另一名词前，表示该名词属于手机的范畴
senses.example: A cellphone camera cannot replace a studio lens.
senses.exampleCN: 手机摄像头无法取代影棚镜头。
senses.why: Nouns in English commonly modify other nouns directly, so cellphone easily becomes a classifier.
senses.whyCN: 英语名词可以直接修饰名词，cellphone 因此常用作限定语，派生出手机电池、手机号码等复合表达。

senses.title: British everyday word
senses.definition: the ordinary everyday word for a mobile phone in British usage
senses.definitionCN: 英国日常口语中对移动电话的普通叫法
senses.example: Switch your cellphone off in the cinema, please.
senses.exampleCN: 在影院里请把手机关掉。
senses.why: Different regions fixed on different names: Britain said cellphone, America preferred cell phone or cellular phone.
senses.whyCN: 各地对同一设备固定了不同叫法：英国常说 cellphone，美国多用 cell phone 或 cellular phone，形成地域变体。

senses.title: A symbol of constant contact
senses.definition: the idea of being always reachable, considered figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 比喻意义上「随时可以被联系到」的状态
senses.example: The cellphone has erased the border between office and home.
senses.exampleCN: 手机抹去了办公室与家之间的界限。
senses.why: Because the device never leaves the owner, it becomes a ready symbol for endless reachability.
senses.whyCN: 由于手机从不离身，它自然成为「随时在线、无法断联」这种现代处境的象征。

senses.title: The object in rules and bans
senses.titleCN: 规章中的手机（禁用对象）
senses.definition: the device mentioned in rules about where it may or may not be used
senses.definitionCN: 在各类场所规章里被点名允许或禁止使用的设备
senses.example: Cellphones are banned in the examination hall.
senses.exampleCN: 考场内禁止使用手机。
senses.why: When a device becomes common enough to cause problems, institutions name it in their rules.
senses.whyCN: 当设备普及到需要管理时，规章便直接点名它，于是 cellphone 在禁令、条款类语境中高频出现。

intro.en: Cellphone is a modern compound, but both halves are old: cell from Latin cella, phone from Greek phōnē.
intro.cn: cellphone 是现代合成词，但两个成分都很古老：cell 来自拉丁语 cella，phone 来自希腊语 phōnē。

items.en: The root *(s)kel-, generally reconstructed, meant to bend or turn; it later fed words for small enclosed spaces.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *(s)kel- 义为「弯曲、转动」，后来衍生出表示「小隔间」的一族词。

items.en: Latin cella meant a small room or storeroom, such as a monk's cell; it also gave biological cell.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cella 指小房间、储藏室（如僧侣的小室），生物学里的「细胞」cell 亦出于此。

items.en: Greek phōnē meant voice or sound; it reached English through telephone, coined in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 希腊语 phōnē 义为「声音、嗓音」，经十九世纪新造的 telephone 进入英语的构词系统。

items.en: Engineers divided a coverage area into small zones called cells, each with its own transmitter; the network was called cellular.
items.cn: 工程师把覆盖区划分为多个小服务区，每个小区设一台发射机，这种网被称为「蜂窝网」cellular。

items.en: As handsets spread, cell phone and cellphone were clipped from cellular telephone and quickly became the everyday words.
items.cn: 随手持电话普及，cellular telephone 被截短为 cell phone / cellphone，迅速成为日常叫法。

items.en: British spelling settled on one word cellphone, while American writing often keeps the two-word cell phone.
items.cn: 英式拼写定型为合写的 cellphone，美式书面语则常保留分写的 cell phone。

note.en: Compare the members of the cell family and the near-synonyms for a hand-carried phone.
note.cn: 对比 cell 词族各成员，以及表示「手提电话」的近义说法。

normalIntro.en: Build the word from its two old parts and the network idea behind them.
normalIntro.cn: 从两个古老成分和背后的蜂窝网概念来搭建这个词。

normal.en: cell = Latin cella, a small room; each radio zone is one small room of the network.
normal.cn: cell 来自拉丁语 cella「小房间」，网络里每个服务区就是一间小房间。

normal.en: phone = Greek phōnē, voice; the same part appears in telephone and microphone.
normal.cn: phone 来自希腊语 phōnē「声音」，telephone、microphone 里都有它。

normal.en: cellular telephone is the long form; cellphone is the clipped everyday form.
normal.cn: cellular telephone 是完整说法，cellphone 是截短后的日常说法。

normal.en: Hexagon cells packed together look like honeycomb, hence cellular network.
normal.cn: 许多六边形小区拼在一起形似蜂巢，故称蜂窝网。

normal.en: cellphones = cell + phone + s, the plural simply adds the s.
normal.cn: 复数 cellphones 只需在词尾加 s。

abstract.cn: 把城市想象成被切成一间间蜂房，每间房里装着一个小发射器。

abstract.en: Imagine your phone as a bee hopping from cell to cell as you travel.
abstract.cn: 把手机想成一只蜜蜂，你移动时它在蜂房间不停跳转。

abstract.en: One word, one object in the palm: cell plus phone equals the phone that roams.
abstract.cn: 一词一物：cell 加 phone，就是那台会漫游的电话。

examples.en: Please switch your cellphone to silent during the concert.
examples.cn: 音乐会期间请把手机调成静音。

examples.en: He lost his cellphone on the bus and lost all his contacts with it.
examples.cn: 他把手机丢在了公交车上，连同所有联系人一起丢了。

examples.en: Good signal makes every journey feel shorter.
examples.cn: 信号好的时候，每段旅程都显得更短。

sensesIntro.en: From the device itself, the meaning fans out to the person's own phone, the calls, the network, and its figurative weight.
sensesIntro.cn: 从设备本义出发，词义扩展到个人手机、通话、移动通信体系，再到规章与比喻用法。

branches.cn: 背后的移动通信体系及其派生的复合用法

latinIntro.en: The Latin side of the family centers on cella, a small room, which also powers cellular and cell in biology.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语一侧以 cella（小房间）为中心，它同时支撑着 cellular 与生物学里的 cell。

definition_zh: 政治家；从政者；政客（含贬义时指善于权术、重许诺轻原则的人）
definition_en: a person who holds or seeks public office and lives by political activity, sometimes with the implication of manoeuvring rather than principle
core_image: 集市广场上，竞选者站在木箱上讲话，向每个伸出手的人逐一握过去
scene: 集市广场上，竞选者站在木箱上讲完承诺，又向每个伸出手的人逐一握过去。 The politician promised to fix the drains before the winter rains came.
sceneCN: 这里指「担任或谋求公职的从政者」，对应第 1 个义项：以公职身份参与政治的人；句意为这位从政者承诺在冬雨到来之前修好排水。画面要点：木箱讲台、人群、握手动作；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A holder or seeker of public office
senses.definition: a person who occupies an elected or appointed office in government or is running for one
senses.definitionCN: 在政府中担任经选举或任命产生的职位、正在竞选这类职位的人
senses.example: The politician promised to fix the drains before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这位从政者承诺在入冬前修好排水。
senses.why: the suffix marks the practitioner of the activity named by the stem, so the word literally means one who does civic politics.
senses.whyCN: 后缀标记的是词干所指活动的从业者，因此这个词字面上就是一个做城邦政治的人。

senses.title: One who lives by politics as a trade
senses.definition: a person whose income, identity and daily work come from political activity rather than from another profession
senses.definitionCN: 收入、身份与日常工作都来自政治活动、而非另一门职业的人
senses.example: He had been a politician for thirty years and had never held another job.
senses.exampleCN: 他做了三十年从政者，从未干过别的工作。
senses.why: an activity becomes a trade when it supports a life, and the word then carries the neutral sense of a profession.
senses.whyCN: 一项活动一旦能养活一个人，就成了职业，这个词也就带上中性的职业含义。

senses.title: The pejorative reading: a dealer in promises
senses.titleCN: 贬义：只会许诺与算计的人
senses.definition: a person seen as caring more about advantage and image than about doing what is right
senses.definitionCN: 被认为更在意利益与形象、而非把事情做对的人
senses.example: They called him a politician to his face, meaning it as an insult.
senses.exampleCN: 他们当面称他为政客，这词是当侮辱用的。
senses.why: because the trade depends on winning consent, the same word easily slides into a charge of insincerity.
senses.whyCN: 由于这一行依赖赢得同意，同一个词很容易滑向「不真诚」的指责。

senses.title: A local officeholder
senses.definition: a person active in municipal or county government, closer to ward business than to national debate
senses.definitionCN: 活跃于市镇或县级政府的人，离选区事务比离全国辩论更近
senses.example: A local politician opened the new clinic and stayed for every photograph.
senses.exampleCN: 一位地方从政者为新诊所剪彩，每张合影都不缺席。
senses.why: the scale of office is supplied by an adjective, and local names the rung nearest to voters.
senses.whyCN: 职位层级由形容词补出，而「地方的」正指离选民最近的那一级。

senses.title: A party figure who brokers support
senses.definition: a person whose standing rests on organising votes and alliances within a party rather than on public speaking
senses.definitionCN: 地位靠组织党内票源与结盟、而非靠公开演讲的人
senses.example: The party politician settled the nomination in a back room.
senses.exampleCN: 这位党务人物在后台一间屋子里敲定了提名。
senses.why: inside a party the work is counting and trading support, so the word shifts from office to organization.
senses.whyCN: 在政党内部，工作是数票与换取支持，于是这个词从「职位」转向「组织」。

senses.title: A skilled operator in any institution
senses.titleCN: 任何机构里善于运作的人
senses.definition: in extended use, a colleague who wins by alliance and timing inside a firm, school or association
senses.definitionCN: 引申用法：在企业、学校或团体内部靠结盟与时点取胜的同事
senses.example: The department head was a politician long before he held a title.
senses.exampleCN: 这位系主任在拿到头衔之前很久就是个政治人物了。
senses.why: the pattern of allies and rivals repeats at any scale, so the label is borrowed wherever influence is scarce.
senses.whyCN: 盟友与对手的格局在任何规模上都会重演，因此只要影响力稀缺，这个标签就会被借去用。

senses.title: The older reading: one versed in statecraft
senses.titleCN: 旧义：精通治国之术的人
senses.definition: in earlier usage, a person learned in the theory and practice of governing, close to what we now call a statesman
senses.definitionCN: 较早的用法中指通晓治国理论与实务的人，接近今天所说的政治家
senses.example: Sixteenth-century writers praised the politician who could hold a restless city.
senses.exampleCN: 十六世纪的作者称赞那种能稳住躁动城邦的治国者。
senses.why: when the word entered English it named knowledge of civic affairs, and the pejorative tone came later with mass electoral politics.
senses.whyCN: 这个词进入英语时指通晓城邦事务的学问，贬义色彩是后来随大众选举政治才出现的。

senses.title: Abstract: one who turns influence into office
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：把影响力换成职位的人
senses.definition: in general use, anyone who converts personal influence into formal authority over a group
senses.definitionCN: 泛指把个人影响力换成对某个群体的正式权威的人
senses.example: In any club, the politician is the member who knows when to call the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 在任何社团里，政治人物都是那个知道何时该提请表决的成员。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the exchange of influence for authority and lets the state and the ballot box fall away.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只留下「以影响力换权威」这一交换，国家与票箱都退出了画面。

intro.en: Politician is an English noun built on the Greek-derived stem of political with the person suffix -ian, and its meaning has shifted from learned statecraft to electoral profession. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: politician 是英语用 political 的希腊来源词干加表人后缀构成的名词，其含义从「治国之学」演变为「选举职业」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Polis meant a city-state and its citizen body; its deeper origin is not established, and the pre-Greek suggestion is only a hypothesis.
items.cn: polis 指城邦及其公民总体；它更深的来源未得到证明，前希腊语来源的说法只是假说。

items.en: Politikos meant 'of citizens, civic, fit for governing', and the derived art of civic management was called politike.
items.cn: politikos 意为「公民的、城邦的、适于治理的」，由它派生的治城之术称为 politike。

items.en: Latin borrowed politicus for civil and state affairs, and medieval writers used politica for the study of the state.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 politicus 用于民政与国家事务，中世纪作者用 politica 指对国家的研究。

items.en: The English noun first meant a person skilled in the science of government, often in a neutral or approving tone.
items.cn: 这个英语名词最初指精通治国之学的人，语气常为中性甚至赞许。

items.en: As parties and mass electorates grew in the nineteenth century, the word settled into its modern sense of a person who lives by winning office, and the disparaging tone followed.
items.cn: 十九世纪政党与大众选民兴起后，这个词固定为「以赢得职位为业的人」这一现代义，贬义语气也随之而来。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same stem that are easily mistaken for the person; group two holds labels for people in public life with different shades of approval.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干、容易被误当成本词的词；第二组是评价色彩不同的公共人物称谓。

entries.definition: The activity or field itself; a politician is the person who practices it.
entries.definitionCN: 指活动或领域本身；politician 则是从事这一活动的人。

entries.definition: Describing what belongs to government or power; it cannot stand for the person.
entries.definitionCN: 描述属于政府或权力的事物；不能用来指人。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning shrewd and tactful, not a noun for an officeholder.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为精明得体的，不是指公职人员的名词。

entries.definition: A course of action adopted by a body; it sounds close but names a document or a rule, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 机构采用的行动方针；读音相近，但指的是文件或规则，不是人。

entries.definition: A senior figure respected for judgement in public affairs; the word is almost always a compliment, unlike politician.
entries.definitionCN: 因公共事务上的判断力而受尊敬的人物；这个词几乎总是褒义，与 politician 不同。

entries.definition: A neutral term for anyone currently holding a post; it says nothing about how the post was won or used.
entries.definitionCN: 对现任职位者的中性说法；不涉及职位如何得到或如何使用。

entries.definition: A person who makes laws in a parliament; a politician may serve in an executive post and never vote on a bill.
entries.definitionCN: 在议会中制定法律的人；政治人物也可能担任行政职务，从不参与法案表决。

entries.definition: A leader who wins support by playing on fear and prejudice; it is far harsher than the pejorative use of politician.
entries.definitionCN: 靠煽动恐惧与偏见来赢得支持的领袖；比 politician 的贬义用法严厉得多。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The stem means civic, and the person suffix marks the one who practices civic business for a living.
normal.cn: 词干意为「城邦的」，表人后缀标记的正是以城邦事务为业的人。

normal.en: The family runs political, politically, politics, polity and politicize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括政治的、在政治上、政治、政体与使政治化。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the tone: a seasoned politician is neutral, a corrupt politician is a charge.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示语气：老练的从政者是中性的，腐败的政客则是控诉。

normal.en: The word entered English meaning a student of statecraft and only later became the electoral professional.
normal.cn: 这个词进入英语时指治国之学的研习者，后来才变成选举职业者。

normal.en: The approving counterpart is statesman, which is almost never used as an insult.
normal.cn: 褒义对应词是 statesman，那个词几乎从不被当作侮辱使用。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses slide along one career: the officeholder, the professional, the promise-dealer, the local figure, the party broker, the institutional operator, the old student of statecraft, and finally anyone trading influence for authority.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条职业线滑动：任职者、以此为业者、兜售承诺者、地方人物、党内撮合者、机构里的运作人、旧义中的治国学者，最后是把影响力换成权威的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker on a crate, shaking every hand within reach.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在木箱上的讲话者，把够得到的手都握一遍。

branches.en: OFFICE: the plain reading, a person who holds or seeks a public post.
branches.cn: 职位：最朴素的读法，即担任或谋求公职的人。

branches.en: TRADE AND SCEPTICISM: once politics is a livelihood, the same word can be neutral about the job or doubtful about the person.
branches.cn: 职业与怀疑：政治一旦成为生计，同一个词既可就职业作中性描述，也可就人品表示怀疑。

branches.en: SCALE AND PARTY: the rung nearest the voter and the back-room broker are two ends of the same ladder.
branches.cn: 层级与党派：离选民最近的那一级与后台的撮合者，是同一条梯子的两端。

branches.en: ANYWHERE AND EARLIER: the operator appears in any institution, and the older reading still honours the student of statecraft.
branches.cn: 无处不在与更早用法：运作人出现在任何机构里，而旧读法仍尊重治国之学的研习者。

branches.en: EXCHANGE: strip the state away and what remains is influence turned into authority.
branches.cn: 交换：把国家抽走，剩下的就是影响力被换成权威。

senses.definition: the process of charging someone and pursuing the case in court
senses.definitionCN: 对某人提出指控并在法院推进案件的过程
senses.example: The prosecution began as soon as the evidence file reached the state's lawyers.
senses.exampleCN: 证据卷一交到州律师手中，公诉程序就开始了。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to follow forward, and the legal noun pictures the state following a charge through every stage of a trial.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「向前追随」，这个法律名词描绘的正是国家把一项指控追随到审判的每一个阶段。

senses.title: The prosecuting authority
senses.definition: the body or office that has the power to bring charges
senses.definitionCN: 有权提出刑事指控的机构或部门
senses.example: The prosecution decided not to pursue the minor charge.
senses.exampleCN: 检察机关决定不追究那项轻微的指控。
senses.why: An institution can stand for the act it performs, so the abstract noun also names the office that decides whether to charge.
senses.whyCN: 机构可以代表它所做的动作，所以这个抽象名词也指决定是否起诉的那个部门。

senses.title: The state's lawyers in court
senses.definition: the lawyers presenting the state's case in a particular trial
senses.definitionCN: 在具体审判中代表国家陈述案件的律师
senses.example: The prosecution sat on the left and the defence on the right.
senses.exampleCN: 控方坐在左边，辩方坐在右边。
senses.why: In courtroom speech the abstract noun becomes a collective label for the legal team on the charging side, like defence on the other side.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭用语里，这个抽象名词变成指控一侧律师团队的集体标签，正如另一侧被称为辩方。

senses.title: The decision to lay charges
senses.definition: the moment or act of formally charging a person
senses.definitionCN: 正式对某人提出指控的那一动作或时刻
senses.example: A prosecution at this stage would need stronger evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个阶段起诉，需要更有力的证据。
senses.why: The word covers the beginning as well as the whole case, because a charge is both a single decision and a long proceeding.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既覆盖开端，也覆盖整个案件，因为一次指控既是一个决定，也是一段漫长的程序。

senses.title: Formal carrying out of a task
senses.titleCN: 正式从事、推行某项工作
senses.definition: in formal writing, the carrying out or pursuit of an activity
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文字中，指对某项活动的推行与从事
senses.example: He was praised for the prosecution of his duties during the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 他因危机期间尽责履职而受到赞扬。
senses.why: The old sense of following something forward survives in formal prose, where any duty or study can be prosecuted, not only a crime.
senses.whyCN: 「把某事向前推进」的旧义在正式文字中保留下来：任何职责或研究都可以被「推行」，并不限于罪行。

senses.title: Pursuit or continuation of an undertaking
senses.titleCN: 事业或行动的继续推进
senses.definition: in older usage, the continued pursuit of a war, a policy or a plan
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，对战争、政策或计划的持续推进
senses.example: The history devotes a chapter to the prosecution of the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这部史书用一章讲战争的进行。
senses.why: Before the word narrowed to law, it named any energetic continuation, and military and political writing kept that wider reach.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词收窄到法律之前，它指任何有力的持续推进，军事与政治文字保留了这一较宽的范围。

senses.title: The evidence stage of a trial
senses.definition: the part of a trial in which the charging side presents its evidence
senses.definitionCN: 审判中由指控方出示证据的那一部分
senses.example: During the prosecution, three experts described the damaged wall.
senses.exampleCN: 在控方举证阶段，三位专家描述了受损的墙体。
senses.why: Since the state speaks first, its phase of the trial takes the name of the whole proceeding, a part standing for the whole.
senses.whyCN: 因为国家一方先发言，审判中属于它的那个阶段便取了整个程序的名字，以部分代整体。

senses.title: Pursuit of a claim in older usage
senses.titleCN: 旧用法中对请求的追究
senses.definition: in older legal writing, the pursuing of any claim or suit
senses.definitionCN: 在较早法律文字中，对任何请求或诉讼的追究
senses.example: The record notes the prosecution of a debt against the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 档案记载了对该遗产的一笔债务追索。
senses.why: Civil claims were once prosecuted as well as criminal charges, and older documents use the noun for any claim pursued to judgment.
senses.whyCN: 民事请求一度与刑事指控一样被「追究」，较早文书便用这个名词指任何追究至判决的请求。

intro.en: Prosecution comes from Latin prosecutio, the noun of prosequi 'to follow forward', built from pro- 'forth' plus sequi 'to follow'. The oldest sense is continuation, and law narrowed it to the pursuit of a charge.
intro.cn: prosecution 来自拉丁 prosecutio，即 prosequi「向前追随」的名词，由 pro-「向前」加 sequi「跟随」构成。最古老的含义是「继续」，法律把它收窄为对指控的追究。

items.en: Sequi meant to follow. It also stands behind sequence, consecutive and the second half of prosecute, showing how widely the idea of following spread.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟随。它也是 sequence、consecutive 以及 prosecute 后半的来源，可见「跟随」这一观念散布之广。

items.en: Pro- 'forth' plus sequi gave prosequi, 'to follow forward, to pursue, to continue'. In legal use it meant to pursue a charge or a claim.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 sequi 构成 prosequi，意为向前追随、追求、继续。在法律用法中指追究一项指控或请求。

items.en: The noun prosecutio named the following or the pursuing, and could describe the continuation of any undertaking, not only a legal one.
items.cn: 名词 prosecutio 指追随或追究，可描述任何事业的继续，而不仅限于法律事务。

items.en: French legal usage applied the noun to the conduct of a case, and English borrowed it with that narrower focus already attached.
items.cn: 法语法律用法把这个名词用于案件进行，英语借入时已带着这一较窄的侧重。

items.en: English used prosecution for both the conduct of a criminal case and the carrying on of any business, keeping the two senses side by side for centuries.
items.cn: 英语用 prosecution 既指刑事案件的进行，也指任何事务的推行，两个含义并行了数百年。

items.en: Modern English centres the word on criminal proceedings, while the 'carrying out' sense survives in formal phrases about duties, studies or a war.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词的中心放在刑事程序上，而「推行」义保存在关于职责、研究或战争的正式说法里。

note.en: Group one separates the related verb and agent from a near look-alike with a hostile prefix and from a word that only shares spelling; group two sets the proceeding against the other names for a case.
note.cn: 第一组区分同根动词与施事者、一个带敌对前缀的形近词，以及一个只是拼写相近的词；第二组把这个程序与案件的其他名目作对照。

entries.definition: To bring and conduct the case; prosecution is the proceeding as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指提起并推进案件；prosecution 指整个程序。

entries.definition: The lawyer who conducts the case; the prosecution can also mean the team or the proceeding.
entries.definitionCN: 指推进案件的律师；prosecution 也可指团队或程序。

entries.definition: Systematic mistreatment, from per- 'through' plus the same following verb; the prefix makes it harassment, not litigation.
entries.definitionCN: 系统性迫害，由 per-「贯穿」加同一个「跟随」动词构成；前缀使它成为迫害，而不是诉讼。

entries.definition: A ban or outlawry, from proscribere 'to write up publicly'; it shares the opening letters but not the following verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指禁令或剥夺公权，来自 proscribere「公开书写」；它与本词只共享开头字母，并不共享「跟随」动词。

entries.definition: Relating to a prosecutor or the conduct of a prosecution, not the proceeding itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指与检察官或起诉行为有关的，不是程序本身。

entries.definition: The court hearing where evidence is tested; prosecution is the pursuing of the charge, which may end before trial.
entries.definitionCN: 指检验证据的庭审；prosecution 指对指控的追究，可能在开庭前就结束。

entries.definition: The whole matter before a court, civil or criminal; prosecution belongs to the criminal side.
entries.definitionCN: 指提交法院的整个事项，民事刑事皆可；prosecution 属刑事一侧。

entries.definition: The formal steps of a legal action; prosecution is the state's pursuit of a charge within them.
entries.definitionCN: 指法律行动的一系列正式步骤；prosecution 是其中对指控的国家追究。

entries.definition: The formal accusation itself, often after a grand jury; prosecution is the process that follows it.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式指控文书本身，常在大陪审团之后；prosecution 是随后展开的程序。

entries.definition: A lawsuit in civil law or a military engagement; in legal speech it is broader and often civil.
entries.definitionCN: 指民事法中的诉讼，或军事行动；在法律用语中范围更广，且常指民事。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real following verb, the real hostile prefix and the real procedural pair.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「跟随」动词、真实的敌对前缀，以及真实的程序配对。

normal.en: Prosequi is to follow forward: the state follows its charge from filing to verdict.
normal.cn: prosequi 是向前追：国家把指控从立案一路跟到判决。

normal.en: Persecution has the same following verb but a prefix of 'through': one follows to court, the other follows to harm.
normal.cn: persecution 共享「跟随」动词，但前缀意为「贯穿」：一个跟到法院，一个跟到伤害。

normal.en: Proscription is a look-alike about public writing, not about following.
normal.cn: proscription 是形近词，讲的是公开书写，而不是跟随。

normal.en: The pair is fixed: the prosecution and the defence, charging side and answering side.
normal.cn: 这组配对是固定的：控方与辩方，指控一侧与答辩一侧。

normal.en: The family runs prosecute, prosecution, prosecutor and prosecutorial.
normal.cn: 同族词有 prosecute、prosecution、prosecutor、prosecutorial。

abstract.en: Picture evidence bags laid end to end, forming a path toward an empty chair.
abstract.cn: 想象证据袋首尾相接，铺成一条通向空椅子的路。

abstract.en: Picture a charge as a rope that the state keeps pulling, hand over hand, through every hearing.
abstract.cn: 想象指控是一根绳，国家一场庭审接一场庭审地双手交替往回拉。

abstract.en: Picture one side of a courtroom speaking first because the state is the one that complains.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭一侧先开口，因为提出申诉的是国家。

examples.en: The prosecution rested after four days of testimony.
examples.cn: 经过四天作证，控方结束了举证。

examples.en: Without the second witness, the prosecution would probably fail.
examples.cn: 若没有第二位证人，这场起诉很可能失败。

examples.en: He wrote a book on the prosecution of long wars.
examples.cn: 他写了一本关于长期战争如何进行的书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖诉究神」——把诉状层层剖开、一路追到底 → 起诉、检控

root: 拉丁 prosequi（向前追随、追究）的名词 prosecutio，由 pro-（向前）加 sequi（跟随）构成；古义为「继续、推行」，后收窄为「起诉」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the criminal proceeding, through the authority, the courtroom team, the laying of charges, formal carrying out, the older continuation of an undertaking, the evidence stage, and the old pursuit of a claim.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从刑事程序开始，经检察机关、庭上的控方团队、提起指控、正式推行工作、旧时对事业的继续、举证阶段，最后到旧时对请求的追究。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: evidence bags laid end to end toward an empty chair.
core.cn: 核心意象：证据袋首尾相接，铺向一把空椅子。

branches.en: THE PROCEEDING: the state follows its charge through every stage of court.
branches.cn: 程序：国家把指控追随到法院的每一个阶段。

branches.en: THE THREE FACES: the authority, the team in court and the single decision to charge are one system seen at different distances.
branches.cn: 三张面孔：检察机关、庭上团队与提出指控的那一个决定，是同一系统在不同距离下的样子。

branches.en: THE OLD SENSE: any duty, study or war can be carried forward, which is what the verb meant before law took it over.
branches.cn: 旧义：任何职责、研究或战争都能被推行，这正是法律接管这个词之前它的意思。

branches.en: THE HEARING: the side that speaks first gives its name to the evidence stage.
branches.cn: 庭审：先发言的一侧把自己的名字给了举证阶段。

branches.en: THE WIDER CLAIM: older documents also prosecute debts and civil claims, not only crimes.
branches.cn: 更宽的请求：较早文书也「追究」债务与民事请求，并不限于罪行。

intro.en: Prosecution is a Latin action noun built on a verb of following, so it names a process rather than a person.
intro.cn: prosecution 是建立在「跟随」动词上的拉丁动作名词，所以它命名的是过程，而不是人。

latinIntro.en: Pro- 'forth' plus sequi 'follow' gives prosequi; the participle prosecutus and the noun prosecutio supply the stem, and -tion makes the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: pro-「向前」加 sequi「跟随」构成 prosequi；分词 prosecutus 与名词 prosecutio 提供词干，-tion 构成英语名词。

items.meaningCN: 向前、向外（前缀给动作一个前进方向）
items.example: The prefix points the following forward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「跟随」指向前方。

items.example: The verb names the following.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词命名跟随。

items.example: The compound named the pursuit.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词命名追究。

items.meaningCN: 已追究的（分词提供英语词干 prosecut-）
items.example: The participle supplied the English stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供了英语词干。

items.meaningCN: 动作或过程（名词后缀把动词转成程序名）
items.example: The suffix made a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成过程名词。

items.meaningCN: 对指控的追究（由动作转为整套程序）
items.example: The prosecution lasted a year.
items.exampleCN: 这场起诉持续了一年。

items.meaningCN: 推进案件的施事者（施事后缀把过程转成人）
items.example: The prosecutor stood up.
items.exampleCN: 检察官站了起来。

items.meaning: to bring and conduct a case
items.meaningCN: 提起并推进案件（去掉名词词尾，回到动作）
items.example: They decided to prosecute.
items.exampleCN: 他们决定起诉。

items.meaningCN: 与检察官有关的（形容词后缀把角色转成属性）
items.example: Prosecutorial discretion is broad.
items.exampleCN: 检察官的裁量权很大。
